#en: When the core finally ruptures, its signal dies with a strangled flicker that ripples across local space, peeling back one layer of misdirection; in the static that follows, a buried return route lights up, pointing toward a debris-choked corridor that no chart admits still exists.  \nIt matches the coordinates hinted at in the first corrupted dataslate, the altered ping from the abandoned relay, and the doctored logs taken off that mercenary ruin, tightening the pattern around a single engineer who has been rearranging wrecks into a map only he was meant to read.
zh: 当核心终于爆裂时，它的信号随着一阵被扼住般的闪烁消亡，涟漪般扫过本地空间，剥去一层误导；在随之而来的静电中，一条被掩埋的返程路线亮起，指向一条任何星图都不承认其仍然存在的、堆满残骸的走廊。\n它与第一块损坏数据板中暗示的坐标、来自被弃中继站被篡改的脉冲，以及从那处佣兵废墟取下的被动手脚的日志吻合，把图案收紧到一个工程师身上——他一直在把残骸重新排列成一张只有他才该读懂的地图。

#en:
The vector traces from the deep-orbit grid stitch perfectly into the last known course of the drifting Navy hulk, turning a nameless wreck into a deliberate waypoint rather than random debris.  
Buried within that ship's sealed logs and stripped corridors is where the path ahead will finally sharpen.  

So far the chase has moved from a forgotten cache on a backwater rock, to nervous whispers in a station dive, to an old relay bunker whose scans did not match the official story, and now to a silent warship everyone nearby pretends never passed through their sky.
zh:
来自深轨网格的向量痕迹完美地缝入那具漂流海军船体最后已知的航程，把一具无名的残骸变成一个刻意的航点，而非随机的碎片。
前路将在那艘船被封存的日志与被拆空的走廊里最终变得清晰。

截至目前，这场追查已从一块穷乡岩石上一处被遗忘的藏匿点，走到空间站酒馆里紧张的低语，再走到一座扫描结果与官方说法不符的旧中继碉堡，如今又来到一艘沉默的军舰——附近所有人都假装它从未经过他们的天空。

#en: When the ledger burns out, it does more than erase a lie; its encrypted failsafe kicks a last, panicked transmission into the dark, pinging a forgotten archive node that was never supposed to light up again.  \nCross-referencing the echo with the stray dataslate from that backwater pit and the mismatched logs scavenged at the dead relay, the investigation shifts from vague suspicions of doctored history to a single, concealed records cache sitting just off a well-traveled lane, exactly where a debris engineer with a grudge would hide the first real draft of the war.
zh: 当账册烧毁时，它抹去的不只是一个谎言；它加密的失效保护把最后一段惊慌的传输踢入黑暗，脉冲唤醒一个本不该再度亮起的被遗忘档案节点。\n把这道回声与来自那处穷乡深坑的散落数据板、以及从死中继站捡回的对不上日志交叉比对，调查便从对篡改历史的模糊怀疑，转向一座紧邻繁忙航道的隐蔽记录藏匿点——正是某个心怀怨恨的残骸工程师会藏起这场战争第一份真实草稿的地方。

#en: The readings preserved in the sample are wrong in a very particular way, a faint shudder in the numbers that never should have appeared this close to a settled lane; only someone chasing that flaw across the systems would leave the same signature behind.  \nOnce matched against the redacted incident logs from the sealed lab and the frantic equations recovered from a discarded slate, the pattern turns from coincidence into a trail, hinting that the same unseen hand has been nudging drives toward the edge of stability wherever the data quietly disappears from the record.
zh: 样本中保存的读数错得非常特殊，是数字里一阵本不该出现在离定居航道如此之近处的微弱颤抖；只有追着这个瑕疵跑遍各星系的人，才会留下同样的特征。\n一旦与来自密封实验室被涂黑的事故日志、以及从被丢弃石板中找回的狂热方程比对，图案便从巧合变成一条踪迹，暗示同一只看不见的手在数据悄然从记录中消失的每一处，都把引擎轻推向稳定性的边缘。

#en: Hidden among routine berth records and "lost" docking slips, a handful of ships appear again and again, always waved through early, always bound for the same quiet stretch of space. Neon's ground crews cannot agree on the details, each retelling of the story shifting slightly as if fear is editing their memories, but the tail numbers do not lie. Follow those privileged hulls, and the trail stops being rumor and starts being a route, leading outward from a dead slate in the black toward whoever is rich enough and ruthless enough to bend whole ports around their passing.
zh: 藏在例行泊位记录与"遗失"的停靠单之间，几艘船一再出现，总是被提前放行，总是驶向同一片安静空域。霓虹城的地面人员对细节各执一词，每一次复述都略有偏移，仿佛恐惧在编辑他们的记忆，但尾号不会说谎。顺着那些享有特权的船体追下去，线索便不再是传言，而开始成为一条路线，从黑暗中一块死石板向外延伸，通向某个富有且冷酷到能让整个港口为它的过境让路的人。

#en: When the sample is finally wired into the forgotten relay, its signature ripples through the old arrays like a remembered voice, waking filters nobody has touched in years.  \nFor a moment the station's dead consoles sketch a phantom lane across the stars, aligning stray pings from that first backwater stop with corrupted timings from the quiet lab and the miscounted traffic that bled through this relay before it was officially shut down, all hinting that her route does not follow the published jump chains at all, but runs just outside them where no one bothers to watch.
zh: 当样本终于接上那座被遗忘的中继站时，它的特征像一道被记起的声音般在老阵列间荡漾，唤醒多年无人触碰的滤波器。\n有那么一瞬间，空间站死去的控制台在星空中勾出一条幽灵航道，把来自第一处穷乡停靠点的散落脉冲、来自安静实验室的损坏时序，以及这座中继站在被正式关闭前漏过的错误计数交通对齐，全都暗示她的路线根本不遵循公布的跃迁链，而是紧贴着它们外侧、无人费心看守之处运行。

#en: The vials were never meant to leave a lab, yet here they sit in a courier's locker, labelled with coordinates that mirror a forgotten listening post and a field garden no registry admits exists.  \nWhoever bankrolled Rourke's experiments smuggled the recipe into Trade Authority traffic, trusting routine to hide intent.  \nNow the trail reads clear enough: the altered wildlife at that lonely homestead, the crooked beacon in high orbit, then the derelict tower's stolen cultures, all pointing toward one last, carefully shielded site where theory is already becoming landscape.
zh: 这些药瓶本不该离开实验室，可它们却躺在一名信使的储物柜里，标签上的坐标映照着一座被遗忘的监听站和一处没有任何登记档案承认存在的田野花园。\n无论是谁资助了鲁尔克的实验，都把配方走私进了贸易管理局的货运里，指望例行公事能掩盖意图。\n如今线索已足够清晰：那座孤独农场聚落里被改造的野生动物、高轨道上歪斜的信标，再到废弃塔中失窃的培养物，全都指向最后一处被精心遮蔽的地点——理论在那里已经变成了地貌。

#en: Cracked open in a forgotten office, the logs map freight routes that never appear on Freestar charts, a web of tugs and dead ships converging on the same blind patch of stars. The manifests name Deimos hardware, missing UC pallets, and scrap registered from the farm you just left, all moved under aliases tied to the same shipbreaker. Together with the first stray slate found in deep space, this pattern confirms you are not chasing random smugglers but someone systematically harvesting classified wrecks and erasing the record one garrison, one yard, one quiet outpost at a time.
zh: 在一间被遗忘的办公室里被撬开后，这些日志勾出从不出现于星联星图上的货运路线，一张由拖船与死船构成、汇聚到同一片盲星区的网。舱单上写着火卫二的硬件、失踪的联殖货盘，以及从你刚离开的那座农场登记来的废料，全都在与同一名拆船工绑定的化名之下流转。连同深空中发现的第一块散落石板，这图案证实你追的不是随机走私贩，而是某个系统性地收割机密残骸、并一座驻军、一座船坞、一座安静哨站地逐一抹去记录的人。

#en: Lines of corrupted timestamps and half-erased coordinates bloom across the screen, resolving into a lattice of connection points that all drift toward the same patch of unregistered space, like iron filings leaning into a hidden magnet. Buried beneath diagnostic chatter, a familiar signature routine repeats, the same neural pattern first glimpsed in that quiet research outpost, proving every stolen design and whispered clinic job has been feeding one plan: a single, unseen gathering point where Splice means to bind her scattered clients into something the corps will never own again.
zh: 一排排损坏的时间戳与半被抹除的坐标在屏幕上绽开，解析成一座连接点的格栅，全都漂向同一片未登记的空域，像铁屑倾向一块隐藏的磁石。\n埋在诊断杂音之下的，是一段熟悉的特征程序反复出现——正是最初在那座安静研究哨站里瞥见的同一神经图案，证明每一份失窃设计与每一桩低语的诊所交易都在喂养同一个计划：一处看不见的单一汇聚点，而"拼接"打算在那里把她零散的客户绑成某种企业再也无法拥有的东西。

#en: The log pulls a single crooked thread out of the noise, a series of jumps that all kink the same way around the lanes before vanishing into dead air. It is not a confession, not even meant to be seen, just the leftover imprint of someone quietly teaching ships to forget the safe routes and trust a different hand. Cross-checked with the stray slate from that backwater rock and the convoy reports that blamed "sensor error" just before going dark, it turns scattered misfortune into a recognizable path, and that path points away from every chart the big powers are willing to admit exists.
zh: 日志从噪声中抽出一根弯曲的单一细线，一连串跃迁全都在航道周围以同样的方式扭结，随后消失进死寂的空气里。它不是一份忏悔，甚至无意被人看见，只是有人悄悄教飞船忘记安全航线、信任另一只手的残留印记。与来自那块穷乡岩石的散落石板、以及那些在失联前把原因归咎于"传感器错误"的运输队报告交叉核对，它把零散的不幸变成一条可辨认的路径，而那条路径背离各大势力愿意承认存在的每一张星图。

#en: On the science facility's dimmed terminals, the transfer orders read like quiet abductions, every donor ID ending at the same unlisted destination code that no routine audit ever chased. The pattern is too neat, too methodical, a route carved to move living cargo and records out of UC oversight and into one ghost signature drifting over an ice world. Back at the first garage, there was only a scrubbed table and missing chems; at the Red Mile, falsified deaths and vanished patients. Now the paperwork itself lines up, all arrows finally bending toward a single hidden ward in deep orbit.
zh: 在科学设施调暗的终端上，这些转运命令读起来像一场场安静的绑架，每一个捐献者 ID 都终止于同一个未被登记、从未被任何例行审计追查过的目的地代码。\n图案太整齐、太有条理，是一条为把活体货物与记录运出联殖监管、送入一个漂在冰封世界上空的幽灵特征而雕琢出的路线。\n回到第一间车库，那里只有一张被擦净的桌子和失踪的药剂；在红里，则是伪造的死亡与消失的病人。如今文件本身对上了，所有箭头最终都弯向深轨中一个隐秘的病房。

#en: Wrecked in patrol space, the SysDef hulk still listens, its damaged arrays quietly echoing a single rogue signal that keeps nudging ship registries off-course. If that echo is not mapped and traced here, every future scan will be reading from bent space, not truth, and whoever is riding those distortions will stay a step ahead of every warrant. So far the hunt has turned up a tampered foreclosure notice on a Freestar world, a ghosted data trail in low orbit, and a derelict whose own manifests disagreed with themselves, all hinting at the same careful hand rewriting where people stand.
zh: 这具在巡逻空域中损毁的联殖防务船体仍在倾听，它受损的阵列悄然回响着一个流氓信号，不断把舰船登记档案推离航向。\n若这道回声不在此时此地被测绘并追踪，今后每一次扫描读到的都将是弯曲的空间，而非真相，而骑着这些畸变的人将永远比每一道逮捕令快上一步。\n截至目前，这场追查已挖出一份自由星系联盟世界被动手脚的止赎通知、一条低轨道上的幽灵数据踪迹，以及一具舱单自相矛盾的废船，全都暗示同一只谨慎的手在改写人们所立之处。

#en: The farmhands only see a season that should have failed and did not; you see the same impossible weather curves you pulled from a dead bounty ship and a lonely prefab, now etched into the tower logs above Akila's fields. Hidden among soil reports and rainfall schedules, a single reference to the grid ties every altered sky back to one source, and for the first time the route between her hand on the controls and the worlds she has touched forms a continuous line. The scattered logs, the erased names, the smuggler gossip about manufactured fog all begin to read like one long, unfinished forecast.
zh: 农场工只看到一季本该歉收却未歉收的收成；你看到的却是从一艘死赏金船和一座孤独预制房中提取的同样不可能的天气曲线，如今刻在阿基拉城田野上方的塔内日志里。\n藏在土壤报告与降雨时刻表之间的一处对电网的引用，把每一片被篡改的天空都系回同一个源头，而她那放在控制器上的手与她触碰过的世界之间的路线，第一次连成一条连续的线。零散的日志、被抹除的名字、走私贩关于人造浓雾的闲话，全都开始读起来像一份漫长而未完成的天气预报。

#en: The survey node here sits just outside every standard jump solution, a sliver of math the nav charts politely ignore. Someone has been using that offset to slip in and out of systems without leaving a clean arrival vector, and if this deviation is not pinned down now, every later trace of their movement will vanish into normal drift. Up to this point the trail is a quiet foreclosure reversal in Freestar space, a scratched dataslate on a forgotten rock, a beacon whose timing never matched its traffic, and calibration logs that all share the same tiny, deliberate misalignment in their route data.
zh: 这里的勘测节点恰好位于每一个标准跃迁解之外，是一小片被导航星图礼貌忽略的数学。\n有人一直利用这处偏移在各星系间进出，却不留下干净的抵达向量，而这个偏差若不趁现在钉死，他们此后每一次移动的痕迹都将消失在正常漂移中。\n截至目前，这条线索由自由星系联盟空域中一次安静的止赎撤销、一块被遗忘岩石上被划花的数据板、一座时序与自身交通从不匹配的信标，以及几份路线数据中都带有同样细微、刻意错位的校准日志构成。

#en: The diagnostic flags buried in this stack were never meant for public eyes; they mark moments when the air should have tripped alarms but did not, little pockets of silence where someone overrode the warning. Whoever has been steering atmospheres from the shadows needed a place to test the trick before trying it on whole settlements, and these anomalies read like rehearsal notes. So far the path here has been a lonely outpost murmuring about bad air, a courier whose manifests did not match its route, and a trader's records showing the same engineer's tools brushing past each incident like a ghost.
zh: 埋在这堆数据中的诊断标记本不该被公众看见；它们标出那些空气本该触发警报却未曾触发的时刻，一小片一小片有人覆盖了警告的静默口袋。\n不管是哪个在暗处操纵大气的人，都需要一个地方先试这套把戏，再拿去整座定居点使用，而这些异常读起来就像彩排笔记。\n截至目前，此处的路径是一座低声抱怨空气糟糕的孤独哨站、一名舱单与航线不符的信使，以及一份商贩记录——它显示出同一名工程师的工具像幽灵般擦过每一起事件。

#en: In the relay's recovered stream, one pattern survives the purge: a thin heartbeat of signals looping from dead satellites to a quiet patch of cropland, each pulse whispering the same coordinates through the noise.  \nIt is not enough to name a face, but it draws a circle in space where someone has been rewriting nerves and weather without filing a single report. So far the trail holds a damaged buoy that carried altered medical manifests, a nervous frontier doctor with blood panels he will not explain, and a station whose wiped logs still point their last uncorrupted line toward those silent fields.
zh: 在中继站恢复的数据流中，有一个图案挺过了清除：一道纤细的信号心跳，从死去的卫星循环到一片安静的农田，每一道脉冲都在噪声中低语着同样的坐标。\n它不足以点出某个名字，却在太空中画出一个圆圈——有人一直在那里改写神经与天气，却从未提交过一份报告。\n截至目前，这条线索包含一座载有被篡改医疗舱单的受损浮标、一名有不肯解释的血检面板的紧张边境医生，以及一座被擦净日志的空间站——它最后一条未被污染的行仍指向那些寂静的田野。

#en: The prototype was never meant to be found; it was meant to sit in familiar orbits, doing familiar things, until every captain stopped seeing the tiny anomalies in their jump reports. Studying it where it was first slipped into routine traffic is the only way to understand how she has been bending gravity just enough to hide her corridors inside habit and overconfidence. From that lonely fringe outpost to the jittering transmitter in high orbit and the vault ship packed with nearly matching logs, the pattern is the same: small, repeated deviations tucked into places everyone thought they already understood.
zh: 这台原型本不该被发现；它本该待在熟悉的轨道上，做着熟悉的事，直到每位船长都不再看见跃迁报告里那些细微的异常。\n在它最初被混入例行交通之处研究它，是理解她如何把重力弯折得刚好足以把走廊藏进习惯与自负之中的唯一方法。\n从那座孤独的边缘哨站，到高轨道上抖动的发射机，再到那艘装满几乎相同日志的金库飞船，图案始终如一：微小而反复出现的偏差，藏在所有人都以为早已理解的地方。

#en: Smugglers have been running these lanes so long their stories blur together, but every altered manifest and "forgotten" detour passes through the same hidden junction in their routes. If Vector wanted to steer whole corridors without tripping alarms, he would ride inside habits like these, tucked behind petty graft and routine favors. Unpicking that pattern here is the only way to see which ships were nudged, and in what direction. So far I have a dust-choked dataslate on a backwater rock, an off-kilter beacon in high orbit, and Gagarin crews who swear they were saved by a course change none of them filed.
zh: 走私贩在这些航道上跑了太久，他们的故事已经彼此模糊，但每一份被篡改的舱单与每一次"被遗忘"的绕行，都穿过他们路线中同一个隐秘的交汇点。\n如果"向量"想在不触发警报的情况下操纵整条走廊，他就会骑乘在这样的习惯之中，藏在小小的贪腐与例行的好处背后。\n在此处拆解这个图案，是看清哪些船被轻推、又推向何方的唯一办法。截至目前，我手里有一块穷乡岩石上积满灰尘的数据板、一座高轨道上歪斜的信标，以及加加林星的船员们——他们发誓自己是被一次谁都没申报的航向改变救下的。

#en: The first anomaly in Gagarin looks like nothing at all, just a smear of handwriting on a dispatch wall where routes get adjusted to match whoever is shouting loudest that day. That is exactly why it matters; only here, in the noise and rust, can someone reroute traffic and lives without raising alarms, hiding intention behind bad lighting and overworked clerks. If the pattern that keeps circling back to one quiet hauler and a recovery specialist is real, it started in these corridors. So far all I have are a stray slate off the lanes and cargo tallies that never quite matched the ships that brought them in.
zh: 加加林星的第一处异常看上去什么也不像，只是调度墙上的一摊潦草字迹——那里的航线会被调整成迎合当天嗓门最大的人。\n这正是它重要的原因；只有在这里，在这噪声与锈蚀之中，才有人能在不惊动警报的情况下改道交通与人生，把意图藏在糟糕的照明与过劳的文书身后。\n如果那个不断绕回一艘安静运货船和一名打捞专家的图案是真的，它就是从这些走廊开始的。截至目前，我手里只有一块露出航道的散落石板，以及几份与运来它们的船只始终对不上的货物清单。

#en: When the cache ruptured, the noise on the scopes did not vanish, it collapsed inward, like a ripple running backwards through the void. This patch of orbit was a scar left by some old, bad jump, a place where drives kept bleeding tiny fragments of their routes into the dark. Vector had been using those fragments, shaping them, letting the past nudge ships toward her chosen corridor.  \n\nSo far I have followed a dead stash on a lonely rock, a gutted relay high above, and half-scrubbed reports in New Atlantis; now even the echoes up here are pointing the same way, into a gap the official charts will not name.
zh:
当藏匿点爆裂时，示波器上的噪声并未消失，而是向内坍缩，像一道倒流穿过虚空的涟漪。
这片轨道是某次古老而糟糕的跃迁留下的伤疤，一个引擎不断把自身航线的细小碎片渗入黑暗的地方。
"向量"一直在利用那些碎片，塑形它们，让过去把飞船轻推向她选定的走廊。

截至目前，我已追过一块孤独岩石上的一处死藏匿点、上方一座被掏空的中继站，以及新亚特兰蒂斯城里半被擦净的报告；如今连这里的回声都指向同一个方向，指向官方星图不肯点名的缝隙。

#en: The relay's shell hangs dead against the stars, but its silence is the point; whatever happened here stopped mid-motion, like someone yanked power in a panic and left the machinery steeped in whatever it had just heard. Only by sampling the noise imprint trapped in its systems can I tell where those interrupted signals were headed before everything went dark. Up to now, all I have is a scrap of corrupted navigation data from a nowhere rock and the knowledge that ships began vanishing along the same old war corridors soon after, suggesting someone started bending the lanes long before anyone thought to listen.
zh: 中继站的外壳死寂地悬在群星之间，而它的沉默正是关键；这里发生的一切都在动作中途戛然而止，像有人在惊慌中拔掉了电源，任由机器浸泡在它刚刚听到的东西里。\n只有采样它系统中困住的噪声印记，我才能判断那些被打断的信号在一切变暗之前驶向何处。\n截至目前，我手里只有一块无名岩石上的一片损坏导航数据，以及一个事实：不久之后，飞船开始在同一条旧战争走廊上消失，暗示有人在任何人想到去倾听之前，就已经开始弯折航道。

#en: In a quiet maintenance alcove of the tower, the schematic glows like a nervous system, power lines rerouted into a pattern that is not about efficiency but about pointing away from civilized space. Each junction mirrors those odd outages the technicians grumbled about in passing, forming a corridor of current that leads off the official charts.  \n\nOut on that nameless rock where the first data cache was found, the corrupted recorder in orbit, and the buried references in oversight files all hinted at the same hand; now the conduits themselves confirm that Vector has been building a path, not a random trail.
zh:
在塔中一处安静的检修壁龛里，示意图像一套神经系统般发光，输电线改道成一种与效率无关、只为背离文明空间的图案。
每一处节点都映照着技术员们随口抱怨过的古怪停电，构成一条驶出官方星图的电流走廊。

在那块发现第一处数据藏匿点的无名岩石上、在轨道中损坏的记录仪里，以及在监管档案中被埋藏的引述中，都暗示着同一只手；如今连管道本身也证实，"向量"一直在建造一条路径，而非随机的踪迹。

#en:
Lines of altered routes bloom across the log, overlapping paths you have already walked in empty orbit and hollowed couriers, all bending toward the dust-haze that clings outside Cydonia.  
Each corrected bearing, each trimmed safety margin, forms a spine of numbers that ends where the city's lights thin and traffic control grows lax.  
Whatever doubts spacers whispered about phantom storms and lucky runs, the pattern here is too clean to ignore.  
It matches the first anonymous slate you found in the back end of nowhere, and the courier's dead records, all tracing the same careful hand turning chaos into cover.
zh:
一排排被篡改的路线在日志上绽开，与你在空荡轨道和被掏空的信使飞船中已经走过的路径重叠，全都弯向赛多尼亚城外缠绵的尘霾。
每一处被修正的方位、每一个被削减的安全余量，构成一条数字脊柱，终止于城市灯火稀薄、交通管制松懈之处。
不管太空人们如何低声质疑幽灵风暴与侥幸航程，此处的图案都太过干净，无法忽视。
它与你在穷乡僻壤发现的第一块匿名石板、以及信使的死记录吻合，全都勾勒出同一只谨慎的手在把混乱变成掩护。

#en: A single scuffed invoice, amended three times in different hands, should not matter, yet every altered digit bends the same way, pointing toward a forgotten lane where condemned hulls quietly change owners. Here, among the mispriced cargo and duplicate entries, you finally see the first deliberate kink in the chain, the moment a routine decommission became something else. So far the trail runs from that lonely rock and its careless clerk to whispered yard gossip and a mourning relative's recording, each piece suggesting someone used paperwork and neglect to smuggle one courier, and one shipbreaker, out of official sight.
zh: 一张被磨花的发票，经三只不同的手修改过三次，本该无足轻重，但每一个被篡改的数字都朝同一方向弯折，指向一条被遗忘的航道——那里的废船悄然易主。\n在这里，在错标的货物与重复的条目之间，你终于看到链条上第一处刻意的扭结，那一刻，一次例行的退役变成了别的东西。\n截至目前，这条线索从那块孤独的岩石和它粗心的文书，延伸到船坞里低语的闲话与一位哀悼亲属的录音，每一块都暗示有人用文书与疏忽，把一名信使和一名拆船工偷偷运出了官方视野。

#en: Cracked seals and forged transit marks on the crate turn random smuggling into a pattern; every rerouted shipment traces the same invisible arc through fringe space, always clearing inspection a little too easily. The signatures on those diversions match vessels that never quite appear on public ledgers, pointing toward a quiet corridor where escorts vanish and debts change hands without witness. The freighter IDs echo ones first flagged in that dead slate in the black and again in the crowded port schedules, each new link tightening the circle around the same unseen broker who moves credits and cargo like pieces on a board.
zh: 货箱上开裂的封条与伪造的过境标记把随机的走私变成了一幅图案；每一批改道的货物都在边缘太空中勾出同一道看不见的弧，总是过于轻易地通过检查。\n那些改道上的签名与从未真正出现在公开账册上的船只吻合，指向一条护卫消失、债务在无人见证下易手的安静走廊。\n这些货船 ID 回响着最早在黑暗中那块死石板上被标记、随后又在拥挤的港口时刻表里再度出现的那些，每一个新环节都收紧圆圈，围绕同一个看不见的经纪商——他把信用与货物当作棋盘上的棋子一样挪动。

#en: The place is barely more than a landing pad and a windbreak, the kind of off-map stopwhere smugglers swap crates and no one bothers to sync clocks.  \nThat makes it perfect for testing hardware you do not want tied to any staryard; the firing solutions baked into this rig match the same skewed geometry you have been chasing in misjump telemetry and wreck spreads.  \nIf these numbers line up with the altered routes from that drifting freighter and the agent's half-finished notes, it means the accidents are not just bad navigation anymore, but someone tuning space itself into a weapon and selling the pattern to anyone who pays.
zh: 这地方不过是一个着陆平台加一道挡风墙，那种图外的中转站——走私贩在那里交换货箱，没人费心对表。\n这使它成为测试你不想与任何造船厂挂钩的硬件的绝佳地点；嵌入这台装置里的射击解，与你在错误跃迁遥测和残骸散布中一直追踪的同样歪斜几何吻合。\n如果这些数字与那艘漂流货船被篡改的航线、以及那名特工半途而废的笔记对上，就意味着这些事故不再只是糟糕的导航，而是有人把太空本身调成武器，并把图案卖给任何付钱的人。

#en: The core ruptures in a flare of warped gravity and static, its song cut mid-note; for a heartbeat, every metal beam in the old barracks groans like it is remembering the war. When the distortion fades, buried emitters along the ceiling spit out a last burst of coordinates and timestamps, overwriting dead militia rosters with a single, pulsing route line. Followed back through the clues so far, that line matches the missing tug from the first slate, the altered scrap that surfaced near the farm, and the falsified deployment orders that pulled a Freestar unit off the board at just the right moment for a shipbreaker to work unseen.
zh: 核心在一道扭曲重力与静电的闪光中爆裂，它的歌声在半音处被截断；有那么一个心跳的时间，旧营房里每一根金属梁都在呻吟，像在回忆那场战争。\n当畸变褪去时，天花板上被掩埋的发射器吐出最后一束坐标与时间戳，用一条脉动的路线覆盖了死去民兵的名册。\n沿着目前所有线索回溯，那条线与第一块石板上失踪的拖船、在农场附近浮出的被篡改废料，以及那些把一支星联部队从棋盘上撤走、恰好让拆船工无人察觉地作业的伪造部署命令，全都对得上。

#en: The decoded pattern is less a message and more a tide line: a chain of medical reroutes, emergency diversions, and unsanctioned evac paths all bending along the same quiet arc through this sector. Following it means stepping into the same invisible current that has been carrying altered patients, blacked-out transports, and one tireless medic from crisis to crisis.  \nTaken with the blank orders cached on that forgotten rock and the scrubbed logs from UC hardware adrift nearby, this signal stops feeling random and starts to look like a standing instruction no one ever cancelled, still guiding him toward some final waiting cohort.
zh: 解码出的图案与其说是信息，不如说是一道潮线：一连串医疗改道、紧急转向与未获批准的撤离路径，全都沿同一道安静的弧穿过这个星区。\n顺着它追，就意味着踏入同一股看不见的水流——它一直在把被改造的病患、失去信号的运输船和一位不知疲倦的医护兵从一场危机送向另一场危机。\n连同缓存在那块被遗忘岩石上的空白命令、以及附近漂流联殖硬件中被擦净的日志一起看，这信号不再像随机，而开始像一条从未被取消的常备指令，仍在把他引向某个最终等待的队伍。

#en: When the crate finally yields its data, it is not contraband schedules or weapons routing inside, but a ledger of course corrections: tiny nudges in grav-jump math that keep steering freighters and patrol ships along the same crooked corridor, many of them vanishing at the exact span where official beacons fall oddly silent. Cross-checking those entries against the stray scrap you pulled off that forgotten rock and the garbled log from the dead relay turns rumor into a contour on the starmap, showing how ships are being walked, step by subtle step, toward an unlisted convergence of wrecks hanging just beyond the last marked lane.
zh: 当货箱终于交出它的数据时，里面不是违禁品的时刻表或武器航路，而是一本航向修正的账册：重力跃迁数学中那些微小的推移，持续把货船与巡逻舰引向同一条弯曲走廊，其中许多正好在官方信标诡异地沉默的那一段消失。\n把这些条目与你从那块被遗忘岩石上取下的散落废料、以及来自死中继站的乱码日志交叉核对，传言便变成星图上的等高线，显示出飞船如何被一步步、细微地牵着走向一处未登记的残骸汇聚点——它就悬在最后一条标记航道之外。

#en: The beacon's recording shows more than background static; buried in the calibration logs is a repeating shift in orbital paths, a tiny bend that only appears when one narrow corridor of space is under observation. It is the same deviation echoed in the misaligned storm beacons on that frontier moon, the same timing gap that cut warning audio in the abandoned relay, the same signature hiding inside the failed grav experiments in the empty lab. Together, those fragments now sketch a crude but undeniable trajectory, tracing where someone has been quietly redrawing the safe lanes and waiting just outside everyone else's field of view.
zh: 信标的录波显示的不只是背景静电；埋在校准日志里的，是轨道路径中一处反复出现的偏移——一种只有在某条狭窄空域被观测时才会出现的微小弯折。\n它正是那座边境卫星上错位风暴信标所回响的同一偏差、正是那座被弃中继站中剪断警告音频的同一时序缺口、正是空实验室里失败重力实验内部隐藏的同一特征。\n这些碎片合在一起，如今勾出一条粗糙却无可否认的轨迹，追出有人一直在悄悄重绘安全航线、并守候在所有人视野之外的地方。

#en: Buried in the listening post's forgotten telemetry, a repeating correction sequence surfaces, threaded through years of routine scans like a whisper in static. Cross-referenced with the earlier courier logs and that first stray slate, it resolves into a pattern of jumps converging on the same off-chart sector. The log does not shout coordinates so much as lean toward them, showing where someone has been quietly teaching the network to look away. Taken with the smuggled firmware signatures and survivor testimonies, the trail now narrows from scattered rumors of ghost routes to a single, deliberate path leading out beyond mapped space.
zh:
埋在监听站被遗忘的遥测里，一段反复出现的修正序列浮出水面，贯穿多年例行扫描，像静电中的一道低语。
与更早的信使日志、以及第一块散落石板交叉比对，它解析成一幅跃迁图案，全都汇聚到同一个图外星区。
这日志与其说是在喊出坐标，不如说是在向它们倾斜，显示出有人一直在悄悄教这张网络移开视线。
连同走私来的固件特征与幸存者的证词一起看，这条线索如今从关于幽灵航线的零散传言收窄成一条刻意设计的单一路径，通往制图空间之外。

#en: The only place that makes sense to start is where everyone pretends not to remember what they heard: the bar lights too bright, the music too loud, and captains numbing themselves with cheap drinks and quiet guilt. In that kind of noise, a strange timing in collision warnings or a reroute that arrived a heartbeat too early becomes just another story to laugh off, unless someone is listening for the same pattern over and over. So far I have a scrap of corrupted telemetry, a whispered name that keeps coming back to the same disgraced controller, and rumors that certain routes started bending years ago and never quite straightened again.
zh: 唯一说得通的开端，是所有人都假装不记得自己听过什么的地方：酒吧的灯太亮、音乐太响，船长们用廉价酒和无声的愧疚麻痹自己。\n在那样的噪声里，碰撞警告中一处古怪的时序，或一次早了一个心跳抵达的改道，都只是又一个可以一笑而过的故事——除非有人一遍又一遍地在听同样的图案。\n截至目前，我手里有一片损坏的遥测、一个不断回到同一名失势管制员身上的低语名字，以及一些传言：某些航线多年前就开始弯折，此后始终没能完全回正。

#en: The depot sits where the lanes thin and traffic records grow vague, a forgotten spur of broken loaders and sealed crates that no one bothers to reconcile against official logs. It is exactly the kind of quiet corner where someone who understands grav seams and dispatch timing would test a new vector, nudging routes a fraction off-course until haulers and wrecks alike began drifting toward the same empty coordinates. So far, everything I have pulled together points the same way: a stray slate from nowhere, nervous freight hands whispering about delayed responses, a settler's sky-watching sketches, and now a calculated bend in space itself.
zh: 仓库坐落在航线稀疏、交通记录变得模糊之处，一条被遗忘的支线上堆着坏掉的装载机和密封货箱，没人费心去与官方日志核对。\n这正是那种安静的角落——一个懂重力缝隙与调度时序的人会在这里测试新向量，把航线轻推离航向一点点，直到运货船与残骸都开始漂向同一组空坐标。\n截至目前，我拼起来的一切都指向同一个方向：一块来自无名之地的散落石板、货运工人们关于迟缓响应的紧张低语、一位定居者守望天空的画稿，如今再加上太空本身一处经过计算的弯折。

#en: The residue scraped from incoming hulls carries more than dust; it carries direction. Tiny shards of scorched alloy and frozen vapor show trajectories no honest freighter should ever fly, angling away from charted lanes toward the same dark corner of the system again and again. Mixed wrong transponder pings, misheard dock calls, a few lazy corrections in the traffic logs turned it into background noise until someone bothered to line the fragments up.  \nSo far I have a dead outpost with an orphaned dataslate, conflicting reports from a frontier stop, and now physical proof that ships serving the same invisible route keep returning with the same graveyard clinging to their skin.
zh: 从进港船体上刮下的残留物承载的不只是灰尘；它承载着方向。被烧焦合金与冻结蒸气的细小碎片显示出任何诚实的货船都不该飞出的轨迹，一次次偏离已测绘航道，指向星系中同一个黑暗角落。\n错误应答器脉冲、听错的船坞呼叫、交通日志里几处懒惰的修正，把它混成了背景噪声，直到有人费心把这些碎片排齐。\n截至目前，我手里有一座带着孤儿数据板的死哨站、来自一处边境停靠点的矛盾报告，如今又有了实物证据：服务同一条看不见航线的船只，归来时总是黏着同一片墓场。

#en: The first anomaly has to be chased at its source, before it gets rewritten or buried under newer traffic. Whatever nudged those jumps off true left only a faint distortion in the timings, a tiny echo in the noise that will not survive another round of routine maintenance or quiet sabotage. Reading that echo clean means catching it early, while there is still enough context to tell a deliberate hand from a faulty buoy. So far all I have is this the same crooked drift showing up across different convoys, captains in frontier bars swearing unseen course corrections saved them, and a nervous analyst on Jemison watching entire anomaly folders vanish as soon as someone higher up took an interest.
zh:
第一处异常必须在源头就把住，趁它还没被改写或埋进更新的交通之下。
无论是谁把那些跃迁推离正轨，都只在时序里留下了微弱的畸变，一道不会挺过下一轮例行维护或悄然破坏的噪声小回声。
干净地读出这道回声，就意味着要趁早抓住它，趁上下文还足以分辨一只刻意的手与一座故障浮标。
截至目前，我手里的只有这些：不同运输队中出现同样的歪斜漂移、边境酒吧里船长们发誓是看不见的航向修正救了他们，以及杰米森星上一名紧张的分析员——只要上级有人表现出兴趣，整份异常文件夹就会消失。

#en: The marker is buried in corrupted telemetry and ghosted comms, a single recurring instruction threading through different battles and different ships, all pointing along the same forgotten curve in local space. When you strip away falsified headers and dead transponders, the path it outlines matches the movements of evacuated patients, blacked-out medical transports, and that medic who never stopped following his first set of orders.  \nWe first picked up his scent from an unremarkable cache on a lonely world, then from a gutted hull broadcasting scrambled commands, and finally from a silent UC frame with its logs carved clean, every step tightening the loop around his invisible triage line.
zh: 这标记埋在损坏的遥测与幽灵般的通讯里，一条反复出现的指令贯穿不同的战斗与不同的飞船，全都沿着本地空间中同一道被遗忘的曲线。\n当你剥去伪造的报头与死去的应答器，它勾出的路径与撤离病患的行动、失去信号的医疗运输船，以及那名从未停止执行自己最初命令的医护兵吻合。\n我们最早从一颗孤独世界上不起眼的藏匿点嗅到他的气息，随后是一具广播着乱码命令的被掏空船体，最后是一具日志被削得干干净净、沉默不语的联殖框架，每一步都收紧环绕他那条看不见的分诊线的环。

#en: Down there, the scars in the dirt feel honest. Heat-burned gullies, blasted rock, twin corridors carved over the same poor frontier roofs again and again until the land itself remembers the pattern. If I follow those tracks, I stay with the settlers and the Rangers, closer to the people who bled for someone's test flight. Maybe I learn who Stormline will spare, not just who he is willing to lose.\n\nUp here, in that junk ring, the sky is rigged like a loaded table. Old buoys whispering new numbers, ships nudged into invisible lanes while a Crimson Fleet hull waits to cash in on whoever survives the drop. If I go there first, I follow the money and the killers who bought his math, not the ghosts it left in the dust.
zh: 在下面，泥土里的伤疤显得诚实。被高温灼烧的沟壑、炸裂的岩石、一次次在同一片贫瘠边境屋顶上刻出的双走廊，直到大地本身都记住了这个图案。\n如果我循着那些痕迹追下去，我就会与定居者和游骑兵站在一起，更贴近那些为某人的试飞而流血的人。也许我能弄清"风暴线"会宽恕谁，而不只是他愿意牺牲谁。\n在上面，在那圈废料里，天空被布置得像一张做了手脚的赌桌。旧浮标低语着新数字，飞船被轻推进看不见的航道，而一具深红舰队船体正等着从坠落后幸存的人身上牟利。如果我先去那里，我追的就是钱和买下他那套算术的杀手，而非它留在尘土里的幽灵。

#en: Among the Fundrunner's sealed racks, one ledger stands out, its transfers looping through Deimos long after the ship was declared dead and its accounts supposedly settled. The dates match missing haulers, reassigned escorts, and those quiet inspection runs no one wanted to sign their name to, all terminating in the same scrapyard corridor. It does not name who rode those routes, but it draws a narrow corridor of opportunity, one that required someone with GalBank clearance and mercenary muscle to keep it open. So far the trail is a mislaid slate off the lanes, bad cargo math in Gagarin's bays, and an illicit route sketch from Neon's underside that all point toward the same habit of hiding people inside financial cleanups.
zh:
在资金快船密封的架列中，有一本账册格外醒目，它的转账在该船被宣告死亡、账户据称结清之后很久，仍绕经火卫二循环。
这些日期与失踪的运货船、被重新分配的护卫，以及那些没人愿意签名的安静巡查吻合，全都终止于同一条废料场走廊。
它没有点出是谁走了那些路线，却勾出一条狭窄的机会走廊——维持它需要某个拥有银河银行权限的人与佣兵的拳脚。
截至目前，这条线索是一块露出航道的错放石板、加加林星货舱里糟糕的货物计算，以及一份来自霓虹城底侧的非法路线草图，全都指向同一种习惯：把人藏进财务清理之中。

#en: The array's readings align too neatly with the broken hulls rusting in this yard; every twisted frame here shares the same slight skew in its last recorded jumps, the same quiet push off the official lanes toward some deeper gravity well. Pulling those numbers together at this place, where wreckage and recalculated vectors overlap, turns scattered anomalies into a map that finally points somewhere instead of nowhere. Up to now all I have had are a discarded log on a forgotten rock, convoy manifests that blame phantom malfunctions, a defector's story about stolen Fleet tech, and an orbital sensor hub humming on a frequency no one logs, each hinting that someone has been laying down a second set of paths beneath the Settled Systems.
zh: 阵列的读数与这座场区里生锈的破损船体对齐得过于整齐；这里每一具扭曲的框架，在它最后记录的跃迁中都有同样的轻微偏斜，同样悄然被推离官方航道、驶向某个更深的重力井。\n在这残骸与重算向量重叠的地方把这些数字汇拢，便把零散的异常变成一张终于指向某处而非无从所往的地图。\n迄今为止，我手里的只有一块被遗忘岩石上被丢弃的日志、把故障归咎于幽灵的运输队舱单、一名变节者关于失窃舰队科技的说法，以及一座以无人记录的频率嗡鸣的轨道传感器枢纽，每一处都暗示有人在定居星系之下铺设了第二套路径。

#en: The lattice spills across the Navy console like a spiderweb of sanctioned lies, jump vectors bent carefully around charted lanes to converge on the same blank patch of space every time. Only a warship of this size would be allowed to store an unauthorized route so close to patrol data without triggering audits, which is why whoever plotted it hid behind military encryption and kept their commentary to terse, bloodless notation. Cross-referenced with the stray slate from the backwater shack, the corrupted logs from that drifting hauler, and the pathing anomalies pulled off civilian manifests, the pattern is no longer rumor; it is a repeatable corridor leading away from every accident site and dead transmission you have touched so far.
zh: 格栅像一张由获批谎言织成的蛛网铺满海军控制台，跃迁向量被小心翼翼地绕过已测绘航道弯折，每次都汇聚到同一片空白空域。\n只有这个体量的军舰才被允许在巡逻数据如此近处存放一条未授权路线而不触发审计，正因如此，绘制它的人藏在军用加密之后，把自己的注释压成简短、冷酷的符号。\n与来自穷乡小屋的散落石板、那艘漂流运货船的损坏日志，以及从民用舱单上提取的航路异常交叉比对，这图案不再是传言；它是一条可复现的走廊，背离你迄今触碰过的每一处事故现场与死去的传输。

#en: When the container breaches and the last trace of strange radiation flares against the bunker's old sensors, the system reacts like it has seen this pattern before, quietly flagging a destination it was never meant to reveal. In the afterglow, a buried routine awakens in the base's cracked consoles, spitting out archived handoff logs, medical transport requests, and encrypted route hashes all pointing to the same orbital facility that has been patching up grav-burned crews for decades. So far the trail runs from a nameless rock with a corrupted slate, to falsified cargo records aboard a wandering hauler, and now to a war-era bunker whose own alarms whisper the same name the healers in Deepala's shadow have been muttering off the record.
zh: 当容器破裂、最后一丝古怪辐射在碉堡老旧传感器上闪起时，系统仿佛见过这种图案般作出反应，悄然标出一个它本不该揭示的目的地。\n在余晖中，一段被掩埋的例程在基地龟裂的控制台里苏醒，吐出存档的交接日志、医疗运输请求与加密航路哈希，全都指向同一座几十年来一直修补被重力灼伤船员的轨道设施。\n截至目前，这条线索从一块带着损坏石板的无名岩石，到一艘游荡运货船上伪造的货运记录，如今又来到一座战时代的碉堡——它自己的警报低语着迪帕拉阴影中的医者们一直在私下念叨的同一个名字。

#en: The relay bunker still hums like it is waiting for orders that never came, walls sweating old condensate under dead status lights. Whatever was siphoned out of those wrecked hulls and stored here links the scrap fields to the patrol grid, a chemical fingerprint that should never have been in UC airspace at all. Matching that residue against atmospheric sweeps will show exactly which vector carried it in and out, and no patrol captain can hand wave away that kind of overlap as "sensor drift." So far the trail runs from a forgotten cache on a backwater rock, to a gutted Deimos yard, and now into this abandoned nerve node, each step tightening the circle around one pilot who keeps treating battlefields like they are still his personal worksite.
zh:
中继碉堡仍在嗡鸣，像在等候从未到来的命令，墙壁在死去的状态灯下渗着陈年冷凝水。
无论从那些损毁船体中抽取、储存在这里的是什么，都把废料场与巡逻网格连在一起，是一枚本不该出现在联殖空域中的化学指纹。
把这残留与大气扫描比对，就能显示究竟是哪条向量把它带进带出，而没有哪位巡逻舰长能把这种重合一挥手说成"传感器漂移"。
截至目前，这条线索从一块穷乡岩石上一处被遗忘的藏匿点，到一座被掏空的火卫二船坞，如今又深入这个被遗弃的神经节点，每一步都收紧圆圈，围绕一名始终把战场当作自己私人工作场地的飞行员。

#en: In the noise of Gagarin Landing's traffic streams, the vector stands out like a bad weld someone tried to grind flat and forgot about. Crosschecked against yard shift changes and tug launch times, it reveals a repeating burn that always arcs toward the same patch of dead space, threaded neatly between SysDef patrol windows and corporate shipping lanes. It is not a smuggler's improvisation but a worker's route, laid in pieces by different hands and never meant to be read as one line. So far the chase has scraped a half erased log from a forgotten rock, shipbreaker markings in a gutted yard, buried sensor echoes in an old relay, and a hijacked service feed here in the slums all converging on the same unseen graveyard he still treats like home.
zh:
在加加林着陆点交通流的噪声中，这条向量像一处有人试图磨平却忘了的糟糕焊缝一样醒目。
与船坞班次变化和拖船出港时刻交叉核对，它揭示出一次反复出现的点火，总是弯向同一片死寂空域，整齐地穿在联殖防务巡逻窗口与企业航运航道之间。
它不是走私贩的临场发挥，而是工人的路线，由不同的手一块块铺设，从未打算被当作一条线来读。
截至目前，这场追查已刮出一块被遗忘岩石上一条半被抹除的日志、一座被掏空船坞里的拆船工标记、一座旧中继站里被埋藏的传感器回声，以及贫民区这里一条被劫持的服务馈送，全都汇聚到他仍视作家的同一片看不见的墓场。

#en: Ebbside means people, and people mean mouths that slip when the drinks are strong and the credits are late. If I shake down the right freight clerk or warehouse runner, I might finally put faces and factions to the payments buying her storms. Of course, walking those alleys with her name on my lips risks stirring up everyone who thought they were just paying for "expedited deliveries," not rewriting their skies.\n\nThe orbital node is quieter, less blood and more numbers. If I pull the raw readings from that relic, I could see the full arc of her work in one sweep, every world her corrections keep bending toward. No bribes, no threats, just me, a data core, and whatever failsafes she left behind in an automated system nobody has watched for years.
zh:
埃布赛德意味着人，而人意味着在酒够烈、钱又拖欠时管不住的嘴。
如果我敲打对了货运文书或仓库跑腿，也许终于能给那些出钱买她风暴的人对上脸和派系。
当然，揣着她的名字走过那些小巷，风险是惊动每一个本以为只是在为"加急配送"付钱、而非在改写自己天空的人。

轨道节点更安静，流血更少、数字更多。如果我从那件遗物中取出原始读数，就能一眼看到她那套工作的完整弧线，看到她每一次修正都在弯向的每一颗世界。没有贿赂、没有威胁，只有我、一个数据核心，以及她留在某个多年无人看管的自动化系统里的全部失效保护。

#en: The old relay hangs in a graveyard of abandoned signals, its dishes frozen mid-gesture toward lanes no one charts anymore. If his routes were ever scrubbed from official records, this is where the echoes would have lodged, half-corrupted in buffer stacks and forgotten diagnostic logs. Out here there are no clerks to massage the numbers, no captains to rewrite after-action reports, just raw jump scars burned into hardware and left to rot. So far the hunt has turned up a nameless cache of navigation data on a forgotten rock and stories of a transport that "teleported wrong" near the frontier; whatever is hiding in this dead node will either tie those fragments together or prove that someone has been bending the map for far longer than anyone wants to admit.
zh:
这座旧中继站悬在一片被遗弃信号的墓场中，它的天线停在指向无人测绘航道的姿态中。
如果他的路线曾被从官方记录中擦净，回声就会滞留在这里，半被损坏地卡在缓冲堆栈与被遗忘的诊断日志里。
在这外面没有文书去揉捏数字，没有舰长去改写战报，只有烙进硬件、任其腐朽的生跃迁伤疤。
截至目前，这场追查已挖出一块被遗忘岩石上一处无名的导航数据藏匿点，以及关于一艘运输船在边境附近"跃迁出错"的传闻；这个死节点里藏着的东西，要么会把这些碎片串起来，要么会证明有人弯折这张地图的时间远比任何人愿意承认的更久。

#en: The data burst you pull from the drifting relay is small, almost an afterthought, but its routing tables tell a different story; every falsified storm report you have seen so far passes through the same chain of freighters and agricultural hubs before vanishing toward a narrow band of coordinates no one files on public charts. It is the first time her adjustments, corporate traffic, and off-the-books shipments all share a single path, and someone took care to list the endpoints only as anonymous grid references, trusting that the pattern itself would go unnoticed. From the prefab in the dust to the dead hunter's fractured log and the altered harvests in the frontier fields, every earlier fragment now reads like a rehearsal for whatever is waiting down that line.
zh: 你从漂流中继站取出的数据束很小，几乎是顺带的，但它的路由表讲述着另一个故事；你迄今见过的每一份伪造风暴报告，都要穿过同一串货船与农业枢纽，随后消失在一片没有任何人在公开星图上归档的狭窄坐标带。\n这是第一次，她的修正、企业交通与账外货运共享同一条路径，而某人小心翼翼地把端点只列成匿名网格引用，指望图案本身不被注意。\n从尘土中的预制房，到死去猎人破裂的日志，再到边境田野里被改造的收成，此前的每一块碎片如今读起来都像是对那条线尽头某种东西的彩排。

#en: The last echoes of the detonation fade, but the traffic map does something no one on any bridge has seen for years: the ghost routes start to unravel. Emergency waypoints flicker, then drop, like someone finally cancelled a standing order no one remembered signing. With that core gone, the invisible hand nudging damaged ships and desperate crews along the same crooked arc has lost its grip.  \nLooking back over the trail, the pattern feels less like coincidence and more like choreography: a nameless cache on a dead world, a derelict patrol hull still obeying half-erased commands, a curated war story with one medic conveniently unaccounted for, all pointing to a system that was still quietly steering the wounded toward somebody who never stopped answering the call.
zh:
爆炸的最后回声渐渐消退，但交通图出现了多年来任何舰桥上都没人见过的一幕：幽灵航线开始散开。
应急航点闪烁，随后熄灭，像有人终于取消了某条没人记得签署过的常备命令。
随着核心消失，那只把受损飞船与绝望船员沿着同一道弯曲弧线轻推的无形之手也松开了。
回望这条线索，图案不再像巧合，而更像一场编舞：一颗死寂世界上无名的藏匿点、一具仍在执行半被抹除命令的废弃巡逻船体、一段被精心编排、恰有一名医护兵去向不明的战争故事，全都指向一个仍在悄悄把伤者引向某个从未停止回应召唤之人的系统。

#en: When the beacon finally unspools its data across the forgotten base's old relays, the path it sketches through the stars no longer looks like random noise but a deliberate slipstream that keeps brushing the same empty coordinates. Whatever ship rode that pattern knew exactly where UC eyes could not follow, and the signal's return address repeats an orbital region that matches hushed talk of burned crews and misjump cases diverted to a single, overworked medical station. So far the trail runs from a corrupted slate on a nameless rock, to falsified manifests in a wandering hauler's hold, to half-erased war sims buried under dust each step hinting that someone has been testing routes at the edges of official charts, then checking the damage somewhere just out of UC jurisdiction.
zh: 当信标终于把它的数据铺展到这座被遗忘基地的旧中继站上时，它在群星间勾出的路径不再像随机噪声，而是一条刻意设计的滑流，一再擦过同一组空坐标。\n无论是什么飞船骑乘着这个图案，它都清楚知道联殖的眼睛无法跟随到何处，而信号的返回地址重复着一个轨道区域，与那些关于被灼伤船员、以及被转入某个超负荷医疗站的错误跃迁病例的低语相吻合。\n截至目前，这条线索从一块无名岩石上损坏的石板，到一艘游荡运货船货舱里伪造的舱单，再到埋在尘土下、半被抹除的战时模拟，每一步都暗示有人一直在官方星图边缘测试路线，然后在联殖管辖之外某处检验损害。

#en: New Atlantis is the comfortable choice, which somehow makes it the most dangerous. If Vector poisoned the numbers at the source, the proof is buried under UC badges, Calyx lawyers, and people who would rather lose a few ships in the frontier than admit they missed a flaw in their own house. Digging there means prying up polished floor panels and forcing bureaucrats to look at what they signed off on.\n\nOut in that strange orbit, the stars do not quite sit where the charts say they should. The lane math bends, splits, then re-joins like it is holding its breath, and every spacer who talks about it lowers their voice as if the void might be listening. If Vector is mapping a fault line through the grav lattice, this crossroads is where his theory stops being rumor and starts becoming a route.
zh:
新亚特兰蒂斯城是舒服的选择，而不知为何，这也使它成为最危险的选择。
如果"向量"是在源头下了毒，证据就埋在联殖徽章、卡利克斯律师，以及那些宁愿在边境损失几艘船、也不愿承认自家房子里有缺陷的人之下。
在那里挖掘，就意味着撬开光洁的地板，逼官僚们直视他们签字批准过的东西。

在那片古怪的轨道上，群星并不完全待在星图所说的位置。航道数学弯曲、分岔，随后又重接，像在屏住呼吸，每个谈到它的太空人都会压低嗓音，仿佛虚空在听。
如果"向量"正在重力晶格中绘制一条断层线，这个十字路口就是他的理论不再只是传言、而开始变成路线的起点。

#en: The underbelly calls first. Neon's damp steel bones are threaded with gossip and off-the-books cartography, every backroom broker convinced they own a private map of who gets through and who disappears. Down there, routes are drawn in favors and fear, not ink. If someone has been steering debtors and haulers into Luc's orbit, the pattern will be etched into those whispered corridors long before it ever reached a ledger.\n\nDeimos is colder, quieter, and somehow more honest. Scrapyard light on dead hulls, manifests clinging to rust because no one bothered to scrub them. If there is proof that escorts and assets were "reassigned" long after the books said otherwise, it will be buried in those frozen paper trails, guarded by professionals who understand exactly what a single surviving stamp is worth.
zh:
下层先发出呼唤。霓虹城潮湿的钢骨里穿织着闲话与账外地志学，每一个密室经纪商都确信自己掌握着一张私密的通行与失踪地图。
在那里，路线是用人情与恐惧画出来的，而非墨水。
如果有人在把债务人与运货船引入吕克的轨道，图案会在它抵达账册之前很久，就刻进那些低语的走廊里。

火卫二更冷、更安静，不知为何也更诚实。废料场的光照在死船体上，舱单黏着锈迹，因为没人费心去擦。
如果有证据显示护卫与资产在账面上早已结清之后很久仍被"重新分配"，它就会埋在那些冻结的纸面线索里，由彻头彻尾明白一枚幸存印章价值几何的专业人士看守。

#en: Neon's underbelly is closer, louder, and filthy with the kind of people Rivet used to drink beside. If anyone sold him a new skin for his ship, it is one of those grease-stained ghosts pretending they never heard his name. Down there I would be trading credits and threats in equal measure, following rumors through back rooms and maintenance shafts, trying not to end up as just another unlogged body under the grating.\n\nThe beacon in orbit is cleaner work, at least on the surface. Just me, vacuum, and a string of forgotten traffic updates that might finally sketch his escape vector in hard numbers instead of bar talk. If those timestamps and altered paths line up with what I already pulled from the yard records and that memorial recording, I will know exactly which way he broke from the lanes when he ran.
zh:
霓虹城的下层更近、更吵，挤满了"铆钉"过去常一起喝酒的那类人。
如果有人给他的船卖过一层新皮，那就是那些满身油污、假装从没听过他名字的幽灵之一。
在那里，我会以同等的分量交易信用与威胁，穿过密室与维护竖井追踪传言，尽量别变成格栅底下又一具无人登记的尸体。

轨道上的信标是更干净的工作，至少表面上如此。只有我、真空，以及一串被遗忘的交通更新——它也许终于能用硬数字而非酒吧闲谈勾出他的逃亡向量。
如果那些时间戳与被篡改的路径，与我已经从船坞记录和那段纪念录音里提取的东西对得上，我就能准确知道他是从哪条航道突围逃走的。

#en: The drift lane where this crate hangs is a blind spot, a thin seam between traffic corridors where automated systems shrug and call missing data a rounding error. That is exactly where a pilot like Vector would let his tracks smear, trusting that conflicting manifests and lazy clerks would hide the shape of his jumps. Whatever is logged against this cargo will show which routes were shaved, which ships appeared where no registered path should have taken them, and which direction he is bending reality next. So far the picture is still half-formed: a half-corrupted slate on a forgotten rock, beacon returns that do not match filed courses, and a Trade Authority hull with waste cycles that belong to a different journey entirely, all nudging the needle toward one name and the unnatural lines he draws through space.
zh:
这个货箱所在的漂移航道是一处盲点，交通走廊之间一道细薄的缝隙——自动化系统在那里一耸肩，就把缺失的数据称作舍入误差。
那正是"向量"这样的飞行员会让自己的踪迹模糊的地方，指望矛盾的舱单与懒惰的文书能藏住他跃迁的形状。
针对这批货物记录下的一切，都会显示哪些航线被削短、哪些飞船出现在任何登记路径都不该带它们去之处，以及他下一次把现实往哪个方向弯折。
截至目前，图景仍只成形一半：一块被遗忘岩石上损坏一半的石板、与申报航线不符的信标回波，以及一具排污周期完全属于另一段航程的贸易管理局船体，全都把指针推向一个名字，以及他在太空中画出的那些不自然的线。

#en: The registry is a scavenger's ledger with its teeth pulled, nothing but serials and decommission dates at first glance, but cross-matched hull IDs and transfer notes show a different story: the same drives, the same controllers, vanishing from official scrapping and reappearing off-books near the same quiet stretch of deep space. Only a ship this forgotten, drifting between ports with no one to vouch for its last cargo, could carry a clean copy of the list before the numbers were massaged for auditors and gossip twisted the details into campfire warnings. So far the trail has been a chain of almosts: an anonymous report from a nowhere outpost, a monitoring shack's glitching readings, a freighter whose jump history did not line up with its manifests, a Neon mechanic hinting at "recycled" parts that never hit the yard.
zh: 这份名录像一本被拔掉牙齿的拾荒者账册，乍看只有序列号与退役日期，但交叉比对的船体 ID 与交接备注讲述着另一个故事：同样的引擎、同样的控制器，从官方拆解中消失，又在深空中同一片安静空域附近以账外方式重现。\n只有一艘如此被遗忘、在港口间漂流、无人为其最后一批货物作保的飞船，才能在数字被为审计员揉捏、闲话把细节扭曲成篝火警告之前，带着这份清单的干净副本。\n截至目前，这条线索是一连串的"差一点"：来自无名哨站的一份匿名报告、一间监测小屋故障的读数、一艘跃迁历史与舱单对不上的货船、一名暗示有"回收"零件从未进过船坞的霓虹城技工。

#en: Buried in the maintenance queue for Neon's lower grid, one tiny block of time repeats with impossible regularity, always tied to the same power sectors and always logged under a rotating list of borrowed credentials. The slot lines up perfectly with drift anomalies flagged by the beacons in this stretch of orbit, suggesting someone has been timing their Grav work planetside to match specific windows in the lanes above. If those schedules are being bent around a single pilot's habits, then the pattern here will tell where he likes to jump from, and when. So far the trail has been a scatter of half-truths and omissions: a misfiled crate tumbling between routes, beacon returns that do not match their courses, and hushed talk in Neon's depths about coils that keep going dark on nights when the same nameless ship slips off the grid.
zh:
埋在霓虹城下层电网的维护队列里，一小段时段以不可能的频率反复出现，总是绑定同样的电力分区，总是在一份轮换的借用凭证下登记。
这个时段与这一带轨道中信标标记的漂移异常完美对齐，暗示有人一直在把地表的重力作业时间安排得与上方航道中的特定窗口吻合。
如果那些时刻表是围绕某个飞行员的习惯被弯折的，那么这里的图案就会告诉他喜欢从何处、何时跃迁。
截至目前，这条线索是零散分布的一半真相与省略：一只在航线间翻滚的错误归档货箱、与自身航线不符的信标回波，以及霓虹城深处关于某些夜晚线圈不断变暗、而同一艘无名飞船悄然脱离网络的低语。

#en: Neon's lower decks are a maze built out of denial and side money. If she is bending patrol nets, the proof is in the hands of dock rats and bookkeepers who know better than to talk loud. Down there I would be trading credits and threats in equal measure, wading through forged manifests and half-truths, hoping someone values survival over silence. It is the softer play, if anything about this chase can still be called soft.\n\nThe tower is different. Clean lines, bad conscience. If I hit that, I am going straight at the people who signed off on this nightmare, not just the ones moving crates. Fractured Phalanx on guard means hardened veterans who already chose a side once and will not hesitate to choose it again. The risk is higher, but so is the chance of ripping out the root instead of just trimming the branches she flies through.
zh:
霓虹城的下层甲板是一座用否认与私钱搭建的迷宫。
如果她在弯折巡逻网，证据就握在码头老鼠与账房手里——他们懂得不该大声说话。
在那里，我会以同等的分量交易信用与威胁，蹚过伪造的舱单与半真半假，指望有人把活命看得比沉默更重。这是更温和的一步棋——如果这场追查还有任何部分能被称作温和的话。

塔则不同。线条干净，良心糟糕。
如果我动了它，我就是直冲那些为这场噩梦签字的人，而不只是搬运货箱的人。
有破碎方阵把守，意味着那些早已选过一边、并会毫不犹豫再选一次的老兵。风险更高，但连根拔起的可能也更高，而非仅仅修剪她穿梭的枝杈。

#en: The first solid threads are knotted up around the Drift-Lane Manifests, and every spacer in Gagarin Landing seems to have a different version of how they vanished, which makes them too important to ignore. On paper they are just cargo and route records, but if someone has been bending safe corridors into killing grounds, the earliest fingerprints will be hiding in those entries, half-lost under corrections and redactions. Until I see how the stories match or fail against the numbers, everything else is just superstition in the bar air. So far all I have are repeated mentions of identical routes flown by ships that should never have shared a path, a handful of captains swearing they felt "pulled" toward the same patch of space, and a lingering rumor about an ex-convoy navigator who always seems to know which way the odds are drifting.
zh:
最初几条结实的线头都缠在《漂流航线舱单》上，而加加林着陆点的每个太空人似乎都有一套关于它们如何消失的不同说法，这使它们重要到不能忽视。
纸面上它们只是货物与航线记录，但如果有人一直在把安全走廊弯折成屠场，最早的指纹就会藏在这些条目里，半消失在修正与涂黑之下。
在我看清那些说法与数字是吻合还是相悖之前，其他一切都只是酒吧空气里的迷信。
截至目前，我手里的只有这些：反复提到由本不该共享同一路径的飞船飞过的相同航线、少数船长发誓他们感到被"拉"向同一片空域，以及一则挥之不去的传闻——某位前运输队领航员似乎总能知道胜算正漂向何方。

#en: The manifest is little more than a smuggler's shopping list at first glance, tucked in with routine cargo notes and refuel records that span half the frontier, but the same corridors of mist and storms keep reappearing beside certain hull IDs and departure windows. Somewhere along the line, captains started timing their runs to manufactured weather, then telling dispatch it was just luck and good instincts. Seeing those entries laid out together turns rumor into a map; it proves someone has been selling quiet pathways through fog and cover, and that the same few outposts and stations keep sitting on the edges of those unnatural clouds. So far everything points back to a single hand on the pressure lines: a dead hunter's broken report, crops that grew through drought, and a corporate annex full of climate logs that never matched the sky.
zh:
这份舱单乍看不过是一张走私贩的购物清单，夹在横跨半个边境的例行货物备注与加油记录之间，但同样的雾气与风暴走廊一再出现在某些船体 ID 与离港时段旁边。
不知从哪一环起，船长们开始把航程安排得配合人造天气，然后告诉调度那只是运气加好直觉。
把这些条目摆在一起看，传言便变成一张地图；它证明有人一直在兜售穿过雾气与遮蔽的安静通路，也证明同样那几座哨站与空间站始终坐落在那几团不自然云层的边缘。
截至目前，一切都回指向操纵压力线的那一只手：一份死去的猎人的残缺报告、在干旱中仍抽穗生长的作物，以及一座气候日志与天空从不相符的企业附属区。

#en: The relay bunker is the clean choice, if there is such a thing. Concrete, rust, UC stonewalling; I know how that game plays. If those scan logs left any shadow behind, it will be in the gaps between what the grid admits and what actually crossed its airspace. Digging through half-dead consoles is slow work, but it might put a clear transponder on Rivet and names to the people who helped hide him.\n\nThe harvesting platform is something else. An old ore rig in an asteroid field is where you go when you want ghosts instead of answers. If there is a signal riding that telemetry, it is not just one man steering wrecks, it is a whole corridor being rewritten in the dark. That feels closer to whatever has been eating ships, but out there it will not just be rocks trying to kill me. Anyone who knows about that field is already lying by reflex.
zh:
中继碉堡是干净的选择——如果真有这种选择的话。混凝土、锈迹、联殖的推诿；我懂那套把戏。
如果那些扫描日志留下了任何影子，它就会藏在网格承认的东西与实际穿过其空域的东西之间的缝隙里。
在濒死的控制台里挖掘是慢工，但也许能给"铆钉"安上一枚清晰的应答器，并给那些帮他藏身的人安上名字。

采集平台则是另一回事。小行星带里一座旧矿石钻井，是你想要幽灵而非答案时会去的地方。
如果有信号骑在那道遥测上，那就不是一个人在操纵残骸，而是整条走廊正在黑暗中被重写。
那感觉更贴近一直在吞噬飞船的东西，但在那里，想杀我的不会只是岩石。任何知道那片场区的人，早就出于本能地在撒谎。

#en: That relay husk sits right where the map starts to lie, a kink nobody claims but everyone routes around. Cipher Blackfire on the ground means contracts, blind loyalty, and someone with enough money to hire professionals to stand on a corpse of a story. If I crack their filters, I see who approved every nudge, who signed off on turning traffic into targets. High risk, close-quarters, and the chance to put real names on all this drifting wreckage.  \n\nThe beacon is different. No guards, just distance and that thin, insistent song pushing ships sideways. If I tap it clean, I get a direction, not a dossier; I see where she is leaning the entire sky before the next correction locks in and becomes "standard practice." Quieter work, lonelier, but it might be the only way to follow her into whatever off-chart horizon she thinks belongs to her.
zh:
那具中继站空壳恰坐在地图开始说谎之处，一个无人认领、却人人绕行的扭结。
地面上有密码黑火帮，意味着合同、盲目忠诚，以及某个钱多到能雇专业人士站在一个故事的尸体上的人。
如果我破解他们的过滤器，我就能看到是谁批准了每一次推移、是谁签字同意把交通变成目标。高风险、近距离，以及给所有这些漂流的残骸安上真名的机会。

信标则不同。没有守卫，只有距离，以及那首细弱而固执、把飞船推向侧面的歌。
如果我把它干净地接入，我得到的是一个方向，而非一份档案；我能看到她在下一次修正锁定、变成"标准做法"之前，把整片天空倾向何方。更安静、更孤独的工作，但这也许是跟随她进入她认为属于自己的任何图外地平线的唯一办法。

#en: Neon's undergut is familiar rot. Bad lights, worse air, and enough Aurora in circulation that people forget what they signed or scrubbed. If I go back there, I am wading through rumor, half-truths, and clerks whose memories are for sale. The risk is getting buried under someone else's lie, but if those misfiled orders and half-finished recalls line up, they might finally sketch the outline of who started bending routes in the first place.\n\nDeimos is different. Scrapyard dust does not care what story you tell about a ship, the metal keeps its own. The Hellbound Dustwalkers are a problem, but at least their greed is honest; they will trade truth if the price is right. If that registry really has the unedited list of where those drives went after they were "scrapped," then it is the first clean spine I can run through all these quiet disasters.
zh:
霓虹城的下层内脏散发着熟悉的腐臭。糟糕的灯光、更糟的空气，以及流通得足够多的极光，让人忘记自己签过或擦去过什么。
如果我回到那里，我就要蹚过传言、半真半假，以及记忆待价而沽的文书。
风险是被别人的谎言埋葬，但如果那些归档错误的命令与半途而废的召回记录对上，它们也许终于能勾出究竟是谁最先开始弯折航线的轮廓。

火卫二则不同。废料场的尘土不在乎你怎么讲述一艘船的故事，金属只保留自己的说法。
地狱尘行者是个麻烦，但至少他们的贪婪很诚实；价钱合适，他们就肯交换真相。
如果那份名录真的存着那些引擎在被"拆解"之后去向的未删改清单，那它就是我能贯穿所有这些安静灾难的第一根干净的脊柱。

#en: The tower is the safer angle, at least on paper. Doors, corridors, hired guns that bleed like anyone else. If I peel back enough of those sealed records, I might finally see who paid for the first trial, who signed off when the numbers started looking wrong, and how a frontier backwater, a broken satellite, and a gutted courier all ended up on the same invisible ledger.\n\nThe beacon is pure Vector. No walls, no cover, just open sky and a sliver of metal humming between grav wells, its pulse bent into a code meant for her and no one else. If I crack that rhythm, I get her routes straight from the source, the timings she trusts with her own life. It is a narrower shot, higher risk, but it points past every proxy and middleman, toward the corridor she has been using to slip just beyond the reach of every faction still pretending they can control this.
zh:
塔是更安全的角度，至少纸面上如此。门、走廊、与任何人一样会流血的雇来的枪手。
如果我把那些封存记录揭开得足够多，也许终于能看到谁为第一次试验付了钱、在数字开始显得不对劲时是谁签了字，以及一座边境穷乡、一颗损坏的卫星和一艘被掏空的信使飞船，怎么会都落到同一本看不见的账册上。

信标则是纯粹的"向量"作风。没有墙、没有掩体，只有开阔的天空与一片在重力井之间嗡鸣的薄金属，它的脉冲被弯折成一段只给她、不给别人的密码。
如果我破解那段节奏，我就能直接从源头拿到她的航线，那些她以性命相托的时序。这是更窄的一枪、更高的风险，但它越过每一个代理与中间人，指向她一直用来滑到每个仍假装能控制这一切的势力触不可及之处的那条走廊。

#en: The barracks route is mud and ghosts. Old drill yards, Wayward Taskforce leaning on rifles and old habits, everyone pretending the scorch marks are just weathering. If there is a paper trail to the patterns, it is probably buried under redacted rosters and casualty drills no one logged aloud. Risk is close-quarters, people who know exactly how I think and move, but the payoff is hard proof: names, orders, something I can point to when the war stories start changing again.\n\nThe asteroid field is colder, cleaner in a way. Just rock, metal, and a listening device tuned to the echoes of every ship yanked a few degrees off-course. No veterans to stare holes through me, only whoever thinks this thing is worth ambushing over. The risk there is subtle: whatever I pull from those grav-wakes will not just confirm a pattern, it will show where all those lines converge next.
zh:
军营路线是泥泞与幽灵。旧操练场、靠步枪与旧习惯撑着的"任性特遣队"，所有人都假装那些焦痕只是风化。
如果这些图案真有一条纸面线索，它多半埋在涂黑的名册与无人出声记录过的伤亡演习之下。
风险是近距离，是那些对我的想法与行动方式了如指掌的人，但回报是硬证据：名字、命令，一些当战争故事再度改写时我能指认的东西。

小行星带更冷、某种程度上更干净。只有岩石、金属，以及一台调谐到每一艘被拽偏几度飞船回声的监听装置。
没有老兵用目光在我身上凿洞，只有那些认为这东西值得伏击的人。那里的风险是细微的：我从那些重力尾流中提取的一切，不仅会确认一个图案，还会显示所有那些线接下来汇聚到何处。

#en: The bunker planetside is slow, stale, and stubborn, like the concrete it is buried under. If I go back there, I am digging through old ghosts and older protocols, chasing anomalies that were never meant to see daylight again. The risk is more about who owned those records than what is guarding them now; step on the wrong file, and UC brass will notice someone is re-opening a story they worked hard to bury.\n\nHigh orbit is cleaner, colder, and sharper. The recon grid will not lie, not the way people do when paychecks and pensions are on the line. Out there, it is just vectors and timing, a map of where a certain rigger threaded the needle through restricted sky and which friendly transponders mysteriously went blind as he passed. The danger is physical instead of political; if anyone else is watching those buoys, they will not appreciate me reading over their shoulder.
zh:
行星地表的那座碉堡缓慢、陈腐而固执，就像它埋在底下所倚的混凝土。
如果我回到那里，我就要翻掘旧日的幽灵与更古老的协议，追查那些本不该重见天日的异常。
风险更多在于那些记录归谁所有，而非如今谁在看守它们；踩错文件，联殖高层就会注意到有人重新翻开了他们费尽力气掩埋的故事。

高轨道更干净、更冷、更锋利。侦察网格不会说谎，不会像人们在薪水和养老金悬于一线时那样说谎。
在那里，只有向量与时序，一张标出某名装配工在受限天空中如何穿针引线、以及哪些友方应答器在他经过时神秘失明的地图。
危险是物理性的而非政治性的；如果有别人也在看着那些浮标，他们可不会乐意我越肩偷看。

#en: That derelict plant down on the rock is the practical choice. Old Fleet math, stolen hardware, rust and dust between me and whatever she took from her own. If I dig it out, I get the before-and-after: where the routes used to run, and the exact moment she started bending them wrong. Less exposure, more time on the ground, more chance to walk out with something I can sell twice if I feel like getting clever.\n\nThat thin strip of orbit is the romantic choice, if you can call it that. No cover out there, just my hull, a twitchy sensor hub, and whoever has been watching the lanes like they belong to them. If I go, I am staring straight at the after: the pattern as it exists now, the invisible hand still pushing ships where they should not go. Higher risk, cleaner answers, and if I am right, I will be close enough to feel whoever built this second map breathing down my neck.
zh:
岩石上那座废弃工厂是务实的选择。旧舰队的算术、偷来的硬件，我与她从自己那里拿走的东西之间隔着锈与尘。
如果我把它挖出来，我就能得到前后对照：航线过去怎么走，以及她从哪一刻开始把它们弯错。
暴露更少、在地面待得更久、更有可能带着某件——如果我动了小聪明还能卖两次的东西——全身而退。

那一条狭薄的轨道是浪漫的选择，如果你能这么称呼它。那里没有掩体，只有我的船体、一座神经质的传感器枢纽，以及某个一直把航道当作自家产业来盯的人。
如果我去，我就是在直视"之后"：如今存在的图案，那只仍在把飞船推向不该去之处的看不见的手。更高风险、更干净的答案，如果我没判断错，我会近到能感到建造这第二张地图的人在我颈后呼气。

#en: The Freestar command trailer is mud, metal, and people who have seen too much go wrong without anyone listening. If I go back there and lean on that deputy, I might finally see whose names are written between his patrol notes, which routes were flagged before someone higher up ordered him to look away. That path smells like politics and buried reports, the kind of truth that gets you locked in a room with a non-disclosure and a smile.\n\nOut in far orbit, the relay and that tired hauler are just ghosts hanging over a quiet world. No briefings, no committees, just raw signal where someone has been carving new lines into the sky. If I chase that lead, I put myself between whoever is buying these lies and the man selling them, with nothing between us but cold vacuum and whatever defenses he thinks are enough. One path walks into offices; the other walks straight into his shadow.
zh:
星联指挥拖车是泥泞、金属，以及一些眼睁睁看着太多事情出错却无人倾听的人。
如果我回到那里去逼那位副手，也许终于能看到他的巡逻笔记之间写着谁的名字、哪些航线在上级命令他别过头去之前就被标记过。
这条路闻起来像政治与被掩埋的报告——那种会让你被关进一间屋子、递上一份保密协议和一个微笑的真相。

在遥远轨道上，那座中继站和那艘疲惫的运货船只是悬在一颗安静世界上方的幽灵。没有简报、没有委员会，只有某人一直在天空中刻下新线的原始信号。
如果我追那条线索，我就把自己置于买这些谎言的人与卖这些谎言的人之间，我们之间只有冰冷的真空，以及他认为足够的防御。一条路走进办公室；另一条径直走进他的影子。

#en: New Atlantis means walking into the beating heart of traffic control and pretending I am just another hauler with time to kill. Manifests, docking logs, customs scans, the whispered side deals in freight offices where clerks know exactly which shortcuts exist and pretend they do not. If there is a paper trail to her corridors, it will be under bright lights and uniformed indifference, buried in arguments over fuel surcharges and who owes who a favor. Safe, on the surface. Loud. Crowded. Easy to disappear in, or be disappeared from.\n\nThe relay in deep orbit is the opposite; no witnesses but whatever sits on that junk hauler's guns and whatever traps she left wired into the beacon's shell. Out there I would be reading her work directly, stripped of official excuses, watching the numbers curve toward whatever she is circling. Quieter, riskier, closer to the bones of the pattern.
zh:
新亚特兰蒂斯城意味着走进交通管制跳动的心脏，假装我只是又一个闲得发慌的运货船司机。
舱单、停靠日志、海关扫描，以及货运办公室里低声的私下交易——那里的文书清楚知道有哪些捷径，却假装不知道。
如果她的走廊有一条纸面线索，它就会暴露在明亮的灯光与穿制服的冷漠之下，埋在关于燃油附加费与谁欠谁人情的争吵里。表面上安全。嘈杂。拥挤。容易消失其中，或被从中消失。

深轨中的中继站恰恰相反；除了那艘废料运货船上的火炮、以及她接进信标外壳里的陷阱，没有别的目击者。
在那里，我将直接阅读她的作品，剥去官方的借口，看着数字弯向她所环绕的东西。更安静、更冒险，也更贴近图案的骨架。

#en: Gagarin Landing is the quiet kind of crooked, the kind that lives in ink and routine. If Vector has friends, they will be the clerks who learned which hulls to wave through and which anomalies to file as "resolved" without looking up. Digging there means talking to people who survive by not remembering too much and prying at patterns buried under years of freight and favors. Safer on paper, maybe, but it puts me in the same room as anyone who profited from looking the other way.\n\nThe recon grid in orbit is a different problem. No bribes, no shrugs, just hard numbers and a lot of cold space between me and whoever does not want those numbers read. If his signature is split across those sensors, it will tell me exactly how he is carving his own lanes and where they bend away from the public corridors. High risk, and if a navy handler notices me snooping, I become the anomaly to erase.
zh:
加加林着陆点是那种安静的歪斜，活在墨水与例行公事里的歪斜。
如果"向量"有朋友，那就是那些学会了哪些船体该放行、哪些异常该在不抬头的状态下归档为"已解决"的文书。
在那里挖掘，就意味着与那些靠不多记、并撬开埋在多年货运与人情之下的图案过活的人交谈。纸面上也许更安全，但它会把我放进与任何靠别过头去获利的人同一个房间。

轨道上的侦察网格是另一个问题。没有贿赂、没有耸肩，只有硬数字，以及我与那些不想让这些数字被读到的人之间大片冰冷太空。
如果他的特征分散在那些传感器上，它就会准确告诉我他如何刻出自己的航道，以及它们在何处背离公共走廊。高风险，而如果某位海军管事注意到我在窥探，我就成了那个需要被抹除的异常。

#en: If I stay in the tunnels, I am chasing voices and paper. The Well stinks of recycled air and rumor, but buried under the gossip and changed stories there is a hard record of what she pushed where and when. Going back into those cramped offices and kiosk backrooms means dealing with people who owe her, fear her, or both but if I want to know who vanished into her promises, their names are written down there somewhere, however deep she tried to bury them.  \n\nIf I go up instead, into that quiet ring of forgotten hardware above the planet, I am chasing the way she bent the sky. No crowds, just old firmware and course corrections that never quite matched their declared targets. If she hid the true map anywhere, it will be in those half ignored survey returns, the ones that kept nudging traffic toward the same blank patch of nothing every time some desperate settler bought hope off the record.
zh:
如果我留在隧道里，我追的就是声音与纸面。深井区散发着循环空气与传言的臭气，但在闲话与被改口的故事之下，埋着一份关于她在何时把什么推向何处的硬记录。
回到那些逼仄的办公室与售货亭后室，就意味着与欠她人情、怕她、或两者兼具的人打交道，但如果我想知道是谁消失进了她的承诺里，他们的名字就写在那里某处，无论她把它埋得多深。

如果我转而向上，进入行星上方那圈被遗忘硬件的安静环带，我追的就是她弯折天空的方式。
没有人群，只有旧固件与那些从未真正匹配申报目标的航向修正。
如果她把真正的地图藏在某处，那就在那些被半忽视的勘测回传里——每当有绝望的定居者私下买下希望，它们就把交通轻推向同一片空白的虚无。

#en: Neon's underbelly is the subtle play. Sit in the smoke, listen more than I talk, let the nav-sellers and data leeches think I am just another spacer chasing a miracle shortcut. If there is a ledger of bent odds and buried corridors, it will be down there, half-encrypted and half-bragged about over cheap liquor. Low profile, high noise, and the kind of place a former convoy navigator could hide behind a hundred other crooks doing the same thing worse.\n\nThe broken command post is the loud option. Burned bulkheads, dead raiders, and a half-finished plan drawn from the same three-forked paths I have been chasing since Gagarin. Going back there means walking straight into someone else's failure, trusting their math and hoping I spot the mistake that got them killed before it repeats. If there is a pattern Vector did not see coming, it is probably scribbled in the margins of those firing arcs.
zh:
霓虹城下层是更微妙的一步棋。坐在烟雾里，多听少说，让那些导航贩子和数据水蛭以为我只是又一个追寻奇迹捷径的太空人。
如果真有一本被弯折胜算与隐秘走廊的账册，它就在下面，半加密、半在廉价烈酒上被吹嘘。低调、高噪声，也是那种前运输队领航员能藏在百来个做着同样事情、只是做得更糟的骗子背后的地方。

倒塌的指挥所是响亮的选择。烧毁的舱壁、死去的劫掠者，以及一份用我自加加林星起一直追查的同样三叉路径画出的半途计划。
回到那里，就意味着径直走进别人的失败，信任他们的算术，并指望我在它重演之前发现让他们丧命的错误。
如果有一个"向量"没有预见的图案，它多半就潦草写在那几道射击弧的页边。

#en: That listening post under the rock still bothers me. Old UC hardware, old protocols, still dutifully recording crossings no one is supposed to make. If I go back down there and dig deeper, I am walking straight into the shadow of classified operations, the kind that erase people for knowing too much. But that file proved she once moved with cover, and if I can untangle who signed off on that, I might learn who is still protecting her.\n\nThe beacon in the asteroid field is different. No flags, no insignia, just raw signals bouncing between frontier air recyclers and an empty point in space. It feels closer to her true work: colonies as lab rats, telemetry as scripture. Following that thread means committing to the idea that she is running her own network now, beyond UC and Freestar, and somewhere out there the endpoint of all these whispers is waiting for someone stubborn enough to trace them in.
zh:
岩石下那座监听站仍让我不安。旧联殖硬件、旧协议，仍在尽职地记录本不该有人进行的穿越。
如果我回到那里挖得更深，我就在径直走进机密行动的阴影——那种会因为你知道太多而把你抹去的行动。
但那份档案证明她曾经带着掩护行动，如果我能理清是谁签字批准的，也许就能知道谁仍在保护她。

小行星带中的信标则不同。没有旗帜、没有徽记，只有在前沿空气循环器与太空中的一个空点之间弹跳的生信号。
它感觉更贴近她真正的工作：把殖民地当实验鼠，把遥测当经文。
顺着那条线追，就意味着接受这样一个想法：她如今在经营自己的网络，超越联殖与星联，而所有这些低语的终点正在某处等着某个固执到愿意把它们追查到底的人。

#en: The schematic is wrong in all the same ways the patrol logs were: tiny offsets, repeated notations, a cluster of emergency waypoints quietly dragged along a single, invisible line through space. Buried in the array's calibration data is a repeating coordinate that does not belong to any regular route, yet every diverted triage run you have traced passes within a hair of it. Whoever set this up did not need orders or announcements; they just bent the infrastructure until wounded crews, lost couriers, and one loyal medic all slid toward the same point without ever seeing the hand on the scale.  \nBetween the anonymous cache, the derelict ship still obeying half-erased commands, and the curated war exhibit that admitted one survivor too many, this misaligned network finally shows the pattern: not random sightings of a roaming surgeon, but a long, slow convergence toward a single, unmarked destination.
zh:
这份示意图错的每一处都与那些巡逻日志一样：微小的偏移、重复的标注，以及一小簇被悄然沿太空中同一条看不见的线拖拽的应急航点。
埋在阵列校准数据里的，是一组不属于任何常规航线、却让每一趟你追踪过的改道分诊航程都擦身而过的反复坐标。
布置这一切的人不需要命令或宣告；他们只是把基础设施弯折，直到受伤的船员、失踪的信使和一名忠诚的医护兵都滑向同一点，却从未看见那只压在秤盘上的手。
在这处匿名藏匿点、这具仍在执行半被抹除命令的废船，与那场恰好多收了一名幸存者的精心编排战争展览之间，这张错位的网络终于显出图案：不是某位游荡外科医生被随机目击，而是一场漫长而缓慢的汇聚，朝向一个未标记的单一目的地。

#en: Neon's underbelly has its own weather: rust, ozone, and the stink of coolant bleeding from mech carcasses no one logged in any registry. If Vector's been ghost-writing guidance logic into scrap and "good-enough" refits, the proof will be in those patched cores, in the way back-alley techs all swear they saw someone fix a ship that was never officially broken. It is closer to the ground, closer to rumor, but also closer to the people whose lives his math keeps nudging.\n\nThe diagnostics wing is cleaner, on paper. Old UC-grade tools, smugglers with ledgers instead of stories, Voltage Hackers selling firmware that somehow matches the same fractional course shifts I have been seeing since that first outpost log. If I can map how their contraband patches spread through Gagarin's manifests, I might finally see the full pattern of lanes he has already bent and the direction his map is still trying to draw.
zh:
霓虹城下层有它自己的天气：锈、臭氧，以及从没人登记过的机甲残骸里渗出的冷却液臭味。
如果"向量"一直在把制导逻辑代笔写进废料与"够用就行"的改装里，证据就会在那些打过补丁的核心中，在后巷技师们都发誓看到有人修好一艘从未被官方认定为损坏的飞船的方式里。
它更贴近地面、更贴近传言，但也更贴近那些生活一直被他的算术轻推的人。

诊断翼楼纸面上更干净。旧联殖级别的工具、拿着账册而非故事的走私贩、出售固件的电压黑客——那些固件恰好与我自第一份哨站日志起一直看到的同样微小航向偏移相符。
如果我能描绘出他们的违禁补丁如何在加加林星的舱单中扩散，也许终于能看到他已经弯折过的航道的完整图案，以及他这张地图仍在试图画出的方向。

#en: If I go back under the city, I am going into his old hunting ground, the place where routine approvals turned into quiet death sentences. Those consoles will not give anything up easily; whatever clerk started pulling on the thread vanished mid-pull, and there is a reason for that. Still, if I want to see the pattern the way he once did, I need to sit where he sat and stare into the same river of numbers until shapes start to emerge.\n\nThe salvage pit is cruder, but honest in its own way. Steel, grease, a nervous dealer who just wants to keep their teeth. If he dumped a datapack there, he expected it to vanish into a tide of broken hardware and desperate hands. That makes it the perfect place to find what he thought was safely destroyed. Follow the shards of his routes through that junkyard, and I might finally see where all these dead colonies, bad beacons, and buried reports have really been pointing.
zh:
如果我回到城市之下，我就要走进他旧的猎场——那里，例行的审批变成了安静的死刑判决。
那些控制台不会轻易交出任何东西；无论是哪个文书开始拉扯这根线，都在拉扯途中消失了，而这是有原因的。
不过，如果我想以他曾经的方式看待这个图案，我就需要坐在他坐过的地方，凝视同一条数字之河，直到形状开始浮现。

打捞坑更粗陋，但在某种意义上更诚实。钢铁、油污、一个只想保住牙齿的紧张商人。
如果他把一个数据包扔在那里，他指望它消失在破损硬件与绝望之手的潮水中。
这使它成为寻找他以为已被安全销毁之物的地方。顺着他的航线碎片穿过那片废料场，我或许终于能看到所有这些死去的殖民地、坏掉的信标与被掩埋的报告，真正指向何处。

#en: The display's holo-panels flicker between heroics and horror, never quite settling on which story they are trying to tell. Tucked beside the sanitized after-action reports is a single cross-referenced citation that should not exist at all, pointing to a restricted patient list and an unacknowledged transfer out of a battlefield that, officially, claimed every soul present. On its own it is just a cataloging error in a floating museum built to make two decades of blood look like necessary history, but against everything else you have seen it becomes something sharper: proof that one medic walked away with his record deliberately bent out of sight.  \nTaken together with the forgotten slate on that backwater rock and the derelict patrol ship still following half-erased orders, this curated footnote finally ties the massacre, the missing triage data, and the roaming surgeon into a single, deliberate omission.
zh:
展柜的全息面板在英勇与恐怖之间闪烁，始终不肯确定自己想讲哪个故事。
在那些经过净化的战报旁，藏着一处本不该存在的交叉引用，指向一份受限的病人名单，以及一次未获承认的、从一片官方声称吞噬了在场每一个灵魂的战场上进行的转运。
单看它，不过是一座漂浮博物馆里的编目错误——那博物馆建来就是为了让二十年的鲜血看起来像必要的历史，但与你看过的其他一切对照，它变得更锋利：证明有一名医护兵带着被刻意弯折、藏于视线之外的记录离开了。
连同那块穷乡岩石上被遗忘的石板、以及那艘仍在执行半被抹除命令的废弃巡逻舰一起看，这处精心编排的脚注终于把这场屠杀、失踪的分诊数据，与那位游荡的外科医生，系成一桩刻意留下的省略。

#en: The spaceport lead is cleaner work, at least on the surface. Sit in the noise, blend with pilots nursing cheap coffee and delayed clearances, peel back the pattern one docking code at a time. If the numbers line up the way I think they will, I could carve straight into the heart of his leverage without ever drawing a gun, just by pulling the right record at the right moment and watching who starts to panic.\n\nThe depot is different. Quiet. Fewer eyes, more rifles. Breakaway Strike Group does not babysit scrap for free, which means whatever crate they are sitting on is tied directly to his favorite routes and the people he pays in blood instead of credits. Following that thread means stepping into a yard full of ex-soldiers with frayed loyalties and long memories, where one wrong question could turn an investigation into a firefight. The payoff there feels sharper, closer to his throat, but so does the risk.
zh:
太空港的线索是更干净的工作，至少表面上如此。坐在噪声里，混在那些捧着廉价咖啡、等待延误放行的飞行员中间，一个船坞代码一个船坞代码地揭去图案。
如果数字如我所料地对上，我就能在不掏枪的情况下，径直切入他筹码的核心——只需在正确的时刻取出正确的记录，然后看着谁开始惊慌。

仓库则不同。安静。眼睛更少，步枪更多。
分裂打击群不会免费照看废料，这意味着他们守着的无论是什么货箱，都直接绑定着他最爱的航线，以及他用鲜血而非信用支付的那些人。
顺着那条线追，就意味着踏入一座满是忠诚涣散、记忆绵长的老兵的场区，一个问题问错，就可能把一场调查变成交火。那里的回报感觉更锋利、更贴近他的咽喉，但风险亦然。

#en: Neon's underbelly is the loudest quiet place I have ever walked. Every storm-crackle through the Span, every flicker of route data on a backroom slate, feels like her handwriting blurred by too many dirty fingers. If I stay down there, I am swimming in rumor and profit margins, trying to pry the truth from captains who like living and brokers who like credits more. The upside is leverage: tug the right ledger, and half the system's smugglers scream at once.\n\nThe deserted relay pulls the other way. Cold metal, dead dishes, a handful of Scrappers who think they own the dark between signals. No noise here, just raw edits, packet scars where official charts were cut and resewn. If I crack that hinge, I see who has really been feeding her the sky and which lanes she is grooming for the next "accident." One path digs into people, the other into the spine of the network; either way, her shadow is getting sharper.
zh:
霓虹城下层是我走过的最吵的安静之地。穿过"跨桥"的每一阵风暴噼啪、密室石板上每一闪航路数据，都像她被太多脏手指抹花的笔迹。
如果我留在那里，我就在传言与利润率的海洋里游，试图从爱惜性命的船长和更爱信用的经纪商嘴里撬出真相。好处是筹码：拉对一本账册，半个星系的走私贩就会同时尖叫。

荒废的中继站则朝另一个方向拉扯。冰冷的金属、死去的天线，以及一小撮自以为拥有信号之间黑暗的拆解者。
这里没有噪声，只有生的编辑、官方星图被剪开又缝回的包体伤疤。
如果我撬开那道铰链，我就能看到究竟是谁在真正把天空喂给她，以及她正在为下一次"事故"修整哪些航道。一条路挖进人，另一条挖进网络的脊柱；无论哪条，她的影子都在变得更清晰。

#en: The bunker lead is the quieter path. Old hardware, old lies, and a deserter who panicked enough to run but not enough to wipe everything. If those scans really caught her crossing restricted air, they are the closest thing to a clean timestamp I am going to get. Paper trails are ugly but hard to argue with once they are in the light. Following that thread means leaning on UC ghosts and hoping the gap in their story finally lines up with mine.\n\nOrbit is the louder option. That cluttered lane, the bored-looking Starblade pretending it has nowhere better to be  it all screams live operation, not leftover debris. If I can peel the cache out from under that escort, I get to see how she plugs a hidden station straight into the spine of the traffic grid. Riskier, a lot more guns between me and the data, but it is the kind of proof you feel through the hull plating when drives start shifting under someone else's hand.
zh:
碉堡线索是更安静的一条路。旧硬件、旧谎言，以及一个惊慌到逃跑、却还没惊慌到抹去一切的逃兵。
如果那些扫描真的拍到了她穿越受限空域，那就是我能得到的最接近干净时间戳的东西。纸面线索虽然难看，可一旦摆到光下就很难争辩。
顺着那条线追，就意味着要倚靠联殖的幽灵，并指望他们说法中的缺口终于与我的对上。

轨道是更响亮的选项。那条拥挤的航道、那艘装出一副无处可去的无聊样子的星刃——一切都在尖叫这是场实时行动，而非遗留残骸。
如果我能从那艘护航舰底下剥出藏匿点，我就能看到她是如何把一座隐秘空间站直接接进交通网格的脊柱。更冒险，我与数据之间多了很多枪，但这是那种当引擎在别人手中开始偏移时，你能透过船壳装甲感到的证据。

#en: The shadows under Neon feel like a confession waiting to be coerced. Power bleeding through cracked conduits, grid runoff carving secret routes for people who live off what everyone else has forgotten. If I go down there, I am wading into gossip and grudges: salvagers who owe her, brokers who fear her, Trade Authority clerks paid to look away. High chance of lies, higher chance of stumbling onto the ledger she keeps in her head, written in the language of outages and missing hulls.\n\nThe beacon in orbit is colder, cleaner, more her speed. Nobody to lean on, just signal and math and the faint tug of an artificial corridor wrapped around a dead grav seam. Track that pulse, strip away the noise, and I might finally see her routes the way she does: as a network of tiny compromises, each reroute and erased queue line bending spacetime toward one inevitable, very personal piece of wreckage she can never stop circling.
zh:
霓虹城下的阴影感觉像一份等着被逼出来的忏悔。电力从龟裂的导管中渗出，电网的溢流为那些靠别人遗忘之物过活的人刻出隐秘路线。
如果我下去，我就要蹚进闲话与积怨：欠她人情的打捞者、怕她的经纪商、被收买而别过头去的贸易管理局文书。
谎言的可能性很高，撞上她藏在脑中的那本账册的可能性更高——那账册用停电与失踪船体的语言写成。

轨道上的信标更冷、更干净，更合她的步调。没有人可以倚靠，只有信号与数学，以及一条人工走廊缠在一道死重力缝上那微弱的拽力。
追踪那道脉冲、剥去噪声，我也许终于能像她那样看待她的航线：一张由微小妥协构成的网络，每一次改道与每一条被抹除的队列线，都把时空弯向一块她永远无法停止环绕的、必然而极其私人的残骸。

#en: Gagarin Landing would mean crawling through the guts of the system itself. Talking to engineers who have forgotten which override was meant to be temporary and which became gospel, digging through tugyard software that has been patched and repatched until nobody remembers what normal looks like. If she baked her tricks into routine maintenance, her trail will be in the calibrations and error margins, not the cargo. Quiet work, technical, but it is where the pattern started to go wrong.\n\nThe depot is the other side of the same trick: not code, but consequences. Forgotten containers, mismatched manifests, guards paid to look bored and never ask why some crates never move. Grid Warbrand being here means someone with money wants those mistakes to stay buried. If I pull on this thread, I am not just chasing a tug's signature; I am putting my nose into whoever has been profiting from every "acceptable loss" along her route.
zh:
加加林着陆点意味着在系统本身的内脏里爬行。
与那些已经忘记哪些覆盖设置本该是临时的、哪些又变成了金科玉律的工程师交谈，翻掘那些被一遍遍打补丁、直到没人记得正常是什么样子的拖船坞软件。
如果她把把戏烤进了例行维护里，她的踪迹就会在校准与误差容限里，而非货物中。安静的技术工作，但图案正是从这里开始出错。

仓库是同一套把戏的另一面：不是代码，而是后果。被遗忘的货箱、对不上的舱单、被收买去装出无聊样子、从不过问某些货箱为何从不移动的守卫。
网格战痕出现在这里，意味着某个有钱人希望那些错误继续被掩埋。
如果我拉扯这根线，我追的就不只是一艘拖船的特征；我把鼻子伸进了每一个一直从她航线上"可接受的损失"中获利的人那里。

#en: Ryujin's tower is the clean cut. Climate control, polished glass, and spreadsheets sharp enough to bleed. If I break into their quiet back-end and pull the right projections, I might see the whole skeleton of his work at once, how corporate appetites and his private triage have braided together. High risk politically, low risk tactically; suits and security cams instead of gunships. If I want proof that this madness has boardroom signatures, this is where it lives.\n\nThat ship is the opposite: no lawyers, just vacuum and metal and whatever guns a nervous captain can afford. The drift pattern matches the diverted traffic like a seam between crimes, a moving hinge he uses to twist routes off their charts. Take that hull apart in orbit and I get something raw, pre-sanitized by any corporate hand. Of the two, it is more likely to shoot first and talk never, but the stories keep pointing to it the way all the dead colonies do.
zh:
龙神大厦是干净利落的一刀。气候控制、光洁的玻璃，以及锋利到会流血的电子表格。
如果我闯入他们安静的后台，取出正确的预测报表，也许就能一眼看清他工作的整副骨架——企业的胃口与他的私人分诊如何编织在一起。
政治上高风险，战术上低风险；对手是西装与监控摄像头，而非炮艇。如果我想证明这场疯狂有董事会的签名，它就住在那里。

那艘船恰恰相反：没有律师，只有真空、金属，以及一个紧张船长买得起的那些枪。
它的漂移模式与改道交通吻合，像罪行之间的一道缝，一个他用来把航线扭离星图的活动铰链。
在轨道上把这具船体拆开，我得到的是生的东西，未经任何企业之手净化。两者之中，它更可能先开枪、从不说话，但所有故事都像那些死去的殖民地一样，一再指向它。

#en: Gagarin Landing is noise and metal and too many eyes pretending not to see each other. The brokers down in the shadow of the Arc Might girders all swear they do not know who keeps rewriting cargo routes, but they all describe the same habits, the same quiet voice that only talks numbers.
