Digging through those forgotten drums and half-buried manifests might finally tie a name to the pattern, but corporate security and desperate salvagers will not like anyone turning over their trash.\n\nThe rock field is different. Out there it is just my hull, the dark, and a signal that should have been switched off years ago. Whatever Vector built into that bend in space, he has been leaning on it for a long time, letting it tug ships off true without anyone noticing. Tapping that signal means fighting off anyone who has learned to hunt its victims, but if I can pull its logs and timing, I might finally see where his routes all converge.
zh:
加加林着陆点是噪声与金属，以及太多假装没看见彼此的眼睛。
在拱力梁投下的阴影里，那些经纪商全都发誓不知道是谁一直在改写货运航线，但他们都描述着同样的习惯、同样的只谈数字的安静嗓音。
翻掘那些被遗忘的油桶与半埋的舱单，也许终于能给这个图案安上一个名字，但企业安保与绝望的打捞者可不会喜欢有人翻他们的垃圾。

岩石场区则不同。那里只有我的船体、黑暗，以及一道多年前就该被关掉的信号。
无论"向量"把什么建进了太空中的那处弯折，他倚靠它已经很久了，任它把飞船拽离正轨而无人察觉。
接入那道信号意味着击退任何学会了狩猎其受害者的人，但如果我能取出它的日志与时序，也许终于能看到他的航线全都汇聚到何处。

#en: The Clinic means people, politics, and a dozen ways this could vanish into committee. If I dig there, I will be peeling back plaques and polite lies, trying to pry a raw truth out from between UC shame and Freestar pride. Risk is subtle: locked archives, quiet pressure, doors that never open again. But if I can find the unedited record of that garrison, I might finally see exactly what was done to him, and maybe who signed off on turning a medic into a weapon.\n\nThe orbit is different. No diplomats, no white coats, just cold metal and whatever is still humming beneath the wreckage. If the infrastructure itself has been bent to keep rerouting the wounded toward a single point, that is where his path is being written in real time. Follow the curve, and I am not sifting history; I am stepping into the same invisible current that has been steering transports, patrols, and him. It feels cleaner, somehow, and much more dangerous.
zh:
星际诊所号意味着人、政治，以及十几种让此事消失在委员会里的方式。
如果我在那里挖掘，我就要揭去一块块铭牌与礼貌的谎言，试图从联殖的羞愧与星联的骄傲之间撬出赤裸的真相。
风险是细微的：上锁的档案、安静的压力、再也不会打开的门。
但如果我能找到那座驻军未经编辑的记录，也许终于能看到究竟对他做了什么，或许还能看到是谁签字同意把一名医护兵变成武器。

轨道则不同。没有外交官、没有白大褂，只有冰冷的金属，以及残骸之下仍在嗡鸣的东西。
如果基础设施本身被弯折，以持续把伤者改道引向同一个点，那么他的路径就是在那里的实时书写。
顺着那道曲线，我就不只是在筛选历史；我正踏进同一股一直在操纵运输船、巡逻队，以及他自己的看不见的水流。它不知为何感觉更干净，也危险得多。

#en: Neon's underbelly is a tangle of bad wiring and worse intentions, exactly the sort of place she would ghost through while the city looks the other way. If I can peel her signal out of the stolen current down there, I might hear what she is planning next, not just where she has been. Of course, everyone who lives off that grid will fight to keep their shadows intact, and walking under the Span with my name on her file feels like asking to be buried in concrete and rainwater.\n\nThe orbital relay is colder, cleaner, all sharp lines and dead metal. If she dumped navigation work in a hurry, it will be up there, stitched into weather telemetry nobody bothers to guard. One quiet sweep and I could see every path she has flown, how the storms, the old labs, and the fuel rigs all intersect. Trouble is, anything sitting in open vacuum this long attracts scavengers and hired guns, the kind who shoot first at anyone nosing around the numbers.
zh:
霓虹城的下层是一团乱麻般的糟糕线路与更糟的意图，正是她会那种在城市别过头去时鬼魅般穿过的地带。
如果我能从下面被偷走的电流里剥离出她的信号，也许就能听到她接下来打算做什么，而不只是她去过哪里。
当然，所有靠那张电网过活的人都会奋力保住自己的阴影，而顶着名字出现在她档案里的我走过跨桥下方，感觉就像求着被埋进混凝土和雨水里。

轨道中继站更冷、更干净，全是锋利的线条与死去的金属。
如果她匆忙丢下过导航工作，它就会在上面，缝进没人费心看守的气象遥测里。
一次安静的扫描，我就能看到她飞过的每一条路径，看到那些风暴、旧实验室与燃料钻井如何在何处交汇。
麻烦在于，任何在敞开真空中滞留这么久的东西，都会招来拾荒者与雇来的枪手——那种会对任何凑近数字的人先开枪的家伙。

#en: Neon's underbelly feels like home and warning in equal measure. Grease, ozone, and too many people pretending not to see each other. If I go back down there, I am trading armor and vacuum for whispers and side-eyes, buying drinks for mechanics who only talk in half-sentences. The payoff is leverage: drive logs, rumors about captains who vanished along the same invisible route, maybe even someone who remembers exactly when a certain calibration tech stopped showing her face and started sending instructions by proxy.\n\nOrbit is cleaner, colder. That beacon and the AR-1006 Warshade smell like the Navy trying very hard not to officially know something. Tackling that lead means hard numbers instead of bar stories, but it also means crossing a line the brass will never admit exists. If I crack their stored vectors, I might finally see the whole pattern at once: civilian wrecks, erased recalls, and one ghost engineer threaded right through the middle.
zh:
霓虹城的下层感觉同等地像家与警告。油污、臭氧，以及太多假装没看见彼此的人。
如果我回到那里，我就要把装甲与真空换成低语与侧目，给那些只说半句话的技师买酒。
回报是筹码：引擎日志、关于船长们沿同一条看不见的路线消失的传闻，也许甚至有人清楚记得某位校准技师从什么时候起不再露面、而开始通过代理发送指令。

轨道更干净、更冷。那座信标和 AR-1006 战影，散发着海军极力想在官方层面不知道某件事的气味。
处理那条线索意味着硬数字而非酒吧故事，但也意味着越过一条高层永远不会承认存在的界线。
如果我破解他们储存的向量，也许终于能一次看清整个图案：民用残骸、被抹除的召回，以及一名径直贯穿其中的幽灵工程师。

#en: The lower levels of New Atlantis feel like his first language. Pumps thrum, people squeeze past each other without looking up, and all the real work happens off any official schedule. If I chase him there, I am walking into the habits that made him, into corridors where a delayed shift change or a locked bulkhead could matter more than any gun I bring. The pay-off is intimate: names, faces, maybe someone who knew him before he started selling empty space for blood.\n\nOrbit is different. Cold, stripped of excuses, every altered course is just math against the dark. If I follow the geometry above that nameless world, I am betting he left one clean record somewhere, a place where his rescues and his traps finally pull apart. Up there I risk Ecliptic, pirates, and whatever "nobody" has been erasing his footprints from MAST logs, but if I am right, the pattern will stop being rumor and start pointing to where he has to stand to keep it all spinning.
zh:
新亚特兰蒂斯城的下层像是他的母语。
泵机嗡鸣，人们彼此挤过而不抬头，所有真正的工作都在任何官方日程之外进行。
如果我去那里追他，我就走进了造就他的那些习惯里，走进那些一条延迟的换班或一道锁死的舱壁可能比我带来的任何枪都重要的走廊。
回报是私密的：名字、面孔，也许还有某个在他开始把空无一物的空间卖成鲜血之前就认识他的人。

轨道则不同。寒冷、剥去一切借口，每一条被篡改的航线都只是对着黑暗的数学。
如果我顺着那颗无名世界上方的几何追下去，我就是在赌他在某处留下了一份干净的记录，一个他的救援与陷阱终于彼此分开的地方。
在上方，我要冒黄道佣兵团、海盗，以及某个一直在把他在三头同盟日志里的足迹抹去的"无名者"的风险，但如果我没判断错，图案就不再是传言，而会开始指向他为了维持这一切运转而必须站的位置。

#en: The relay in the dark between worlds is a wound in the freight network, and the broker sitting in it is the infection. If I lean on him, strip his numbers down to bare timestamps and hull IDs, I might finally see exactly who is paying to move these sealed tanks and where they jump next. It is a dirty play, close-quarters and personal, but every liar I break at that relay narrows the field of people who can afford Catalyst's little experiments.\n\nThe empty orbital lane is cleaner, colder. Out there it is just me, the RD-1964 Scrapviper, and whatever raw vectors it is sitting on. Cut that ship open and I get math, not stories: tanker headings, burn signatures, the precise moment they slip off the public boards. It is higher risk in the short term, Spacers do not scare easy, but the payoff is a direct line to whatever off-grid cistern she is feeding. One path squeezes a human weak link; the other gambles everything on hard data and a gun run in vacuum.
zh:
世界之间黑暗里的那座中继站是货运网络上的一道伤口，而坐在其中的经纪商就是感染。
如果我逼他，把那些数字剥到只剩时间戳与船体 ID，也许终于能看清究竟是谁在出钱运送这些密封储罐、以及它们下一步跃迁到何处。
这是肮脏的一手，近距离且针对个人，但我在那座中继站撬开的每一个骗子，都会收窄能负担"催化剂"那些小实验的人员范围。

空荡的轨道航道更干净、更冷。那里只有我、RD-1964 废料毒蛇，以及它所守着的那些生向量。
把那艘船切开，我得到的是数学，而非故事：油轮航向、点火特征、它们滑出公开公告板的精确时刻。
短期内风险更高，太空劫匪可不容易被吓到，但回报是直通她所喂养的某个离网蓄水池的线。一条路挤压一个人类的薄弱环节；另一条把一切都赌在硬数据与真空中一次枪战上。

#en: The Clinic is the safer play, at least on paper. Clean corridors, regulated air, people paid to pretend none of this is strange as long as the paperwork balances. If his experiments ever brushed living tissue, there will be traces here buried as anonymized scans and misfiled case notes, each one another step in turning a stopgap into standard procedure. Picking this route means talking to professionals who know more than they are allowed to say, and hoping my charm lasts longer than their patience.\n\nThe rig in high orbit is the opposite: no rules, no oversight, just an aging platform and the Riftclaw parked on top of it like a warning. If he really does speak through dead hardware, that beacon is probably one of his favorite throats to borrow. Chasing this thread means trusting gossip and gunplay more than signed records, but the payoff could be a live signal a direct line to where his ghosts actually jump from, instead of the scars they leave behind.
zh:
星际诊所号是更安全的棋，至少纸面上如此。干净的走廊、受监管的空气，以及只要文书平衡就被收买去假装这一切都不奇怪的人。
如果他的实验曾擦过活体组织，这里就会有痕迹，被埋成匿名扫描与归档错误的病例记录，每一处都是把权宜之计变成标准流程的又一步。
选择这条路意味着与那些知道的比被允许说的更多的专业人士交谈，并指望我的魅力比他们的耐心撑得更久。

高轨道上的钻井则相反：没有规则、没有监管，只有一座老化的平台，以及像警告一样停在它上面的裂爪号。
如果他真通过死硬件说话，那座信标多半是他最爱借用的喉咙之一。
追这条线意味着更信任闲话与枪战，而非签署过的记录，但回报可能是一道活信号——一条直通他那些幽灵实际跃迁出发点的线，而非它们留下的伤疤。

#en: Cydonia first means walking into polished stone and recycled air, where the lies wear clean boots and keep their voices level. That functionary with the hidden storage is probably just one of many, but crack their cache and I might finally see how deep the redactions go, who signed off on near-misses and called them acceptable. Less gunfire, more locked doors and careful threats, but if I want names and dates that will stick, this is where they are hiding.\n\nOrbit is the other choice, where the hauler drifts like a bad habit nobody reports. If I shadow that Crimson hull, board it or crack its buffers, I get to see how her bent lanes turn into profit and blood, and which captains pay for the privilege. Risk is higher out there, no bureaucracy to hide behind, just guns and vacuum and the chance the Fleet decides I know too much. But if I want proof she is feeding pirates the same patterns I saw in those old logs, that ship is already moving to the rhythm she set.
zh:
赛多尼亚首先意味着走进打磨过的石头与循环空气之中，那里的谎言穿着干净的靴子、嗓音平稳。
那个藏有暗格的小职员多半只是众多之一，但撬开他们的藏匿点，也许终于能看到涂黑延伸得多深、是谁签字把惊险接近称作可接受。
枪火更少，锁门与谨慎的威胁更多，但如果我想要站得住脚的名字与日期，它们就藏在那里。

轨道是另一个选择，那艘运货船像没人上报的坏习惯一样漂在那里。
如果我尾随那具深红舰队船体，登船或破解它的缓冲区，我就能看到她的弯曲航道如何变成利润与鲜血，以及哪些船长花钱买这个特权。
那里风险更高，没有官僚体制可以躲在后面，只有枪、真空，以及舰队认定我知道太多的可能。
但如果我想证明她正在把我在那些旧日志里看到的同样图案喂给海盗，那艘船已经在她设定的节奏里航行了。

#en: The shack is the safer play, if anything about this mess can be called that. Sit in the dim light, let some nervous broker sweat while I peel his cache apart, see which fragments line up with the telemetry I already stole. If he has a clean clip of her voice riding those strange jumps, I might finally separate superstition from math. The risk is human here everyone wants to own the story, twist it, sell it twice, and I could walk out with nothing but another layer of lies.\n\nThe beacon in the rocks is different. No witnesses, no spin, just raw signal tangled in an old weapons graveyard, exactly the kind of place she would use as a hinge for something ugly. Following that line pins me closer to the truth and to whoever signed off on using ranges as scaffolding for new lanes. But it also means trusting her geometry enough to fly into the scars she favors, and once I commit to that version of the story, there is no pretending this is just about a rogue pilot anymore.
zh:
那间小屋是更安全的棋，如果这堆烂摊子里还有什么能被这么称呼。
坐在昏暗的灯光里，让某个紧张的经纪商冒汗，而我拆开他的藏匿点，看看哪些碎片与我已经偷到的遥测对得上。
如果他有一段她骑乘那些古怪跃迁的干净录音，也许终于能把迷信与数学分开。
这里的风险是人——每个人都想占有这个故事、扭曲它、卖它两次，而我可能带着又一层谎言走出来，除此之外一无所有。

岩石中的那座信标则不同。没有目击者、没有说辞，只有缠在一座旧武器坟场里的生信号，正是她会用来作为某种丑陋东西铰链的地方。
顺着那条线追，会把我更紧地钉向真相，也钉向那些签字同意把靶场当作新航道脚手架的人。
但这也意味着要足够信任她的几何，飞进她偏爱的那些伤疤里，而一旦我认下这个版本的故事，就再也不能假装这只是一个失控飞行员的事了。

#en: If I go back down into the queues, I am walking into the place that shaped her and broke her in the same breath. Faces, not freight, are the currency there. Every name on a slate is a memory of who she helped, who she condemned, and the samples pulled from that mess might finally show me how she stitched all those "exceptions" into a single route. It will be cramped, political, full of people who owe her more than they will ever owe me but if I want motive instead of rumor, that is where it lives.  \n\nThe relay on the moon is colder, simpler. Numbers and vectors, no eyes watching, just cargo streams she bent to feed some canyon no one admits exists. Cracking those ledgers means tangling with smugglers and a Trade Authority parasite who has been skimming her shadow work, but it also means hard proof ships, tags, tonnage, all pointing one way. Down there I might learn why she did it; out here, I might finally see exactly where everything she touched was meant to land.
zh:
如果我回到下面那些队列里，我就走进了那个一边塑造她、一边打碎她的地方。
在那里，通货是面孔，而不是货运。石板上每一个名字都是一段记忆——她帮过谁、她判过谁，而从这团混乱中提取的样本，也许终于能让我看清她是如何把那些"例外"缝成一条路线的。
那里会拥挤、政治化，满是欠她比欠我更多人情的人，但如果我想要动机而非传言，它就住在那里。

月球上的中继站更冷、更简单。数字与向量，没有眼睛在看着，只有她弯折去喂养某条没人承认存在的峡谷的货物流。
破解那些账册意味着与走私贩、以及一名一直在偷吃她影子工作的贸易管理局寄生虫纠缠，但也意味着硬证据：船只、标签、吨位，全都指向一个方向。
在下面，我也许能弄清她为什么这么做；在这里，我也许终于能看到她触碰过的一切本该落在何处。

#en: Gagarin Landing is risky in the loud way. Scaffolds, unions, offworld management pretending the numbers balance while they test whatever they can bolt to a bulkhead. If Vector let someone build from his math, this is where it would sit humming in plain sight, buried behind "efficiency trials" and fake serials. I could shake down riggers, skim diagnostics, maybe even rip the guts out of a prototype, but once I start asking questions here, the people protecting their paychecks will notice fast.\n\nThe research module is risky in the quiet way. No traffic, no oversight, just dead consoles and one person's obsession with a pattern nobody else wanted to see. If the watcher who worked there ever pinned Vector down to something more than a rumor, it will be in those spliced logs and forked route comparisons. Walking that corridor means trusting a ghost's instincts over my own, chasing the exact moment coincidences stopped feeling random and became someone's deliberate curve through space.
zh:
加加林着陆点的风险是响亮的那种。脚手架、工会，以及一边假装数字平衡、一边测试他们能往舱壁上拴什么的境外管理层。
如果"向量"让人按他的数学建造过什么，它就会在众目睽睽之下嗡鸣，藏在"效率试验"与假序列号之后。
我可以敲打装配工、偷看诊断，甚至把一具原型开膛破肚，但一旦我在这里开始提问，那些守护自己薪水的人很快就会注意到。

研究模块的风险是安静的那种。没有交通、没有监管，只有死去的控制台，以及一个人对某个别人不想看的图案的执念。
如果在那里工作过的那位观察者曾把"向量"从传言钉成更实在的东西，它就会在那些拼接日志与分叉航线比对里。
走过那条走廊，意味着要相信一个幽灵的直觉胜过自己的，去追那段巧合不再感觉随机、而变成某人刻意穿越太空的曲线的确切时刻。

#en: Neon's rooftops are a bad place to think straight. Every arc of lightning through the Grid, every forgotten landing ping nudging ships the same way, feels like standing inside his skull while it dreams. If I follow that line, I am betting that the city's old habits and his new edits are now the same thing, that the pulse over Volii is the heartbeat of his favorite escape route. It is risk wrapped in noise and corporate shadows, but if he is still tuning the sky anywhere, it will be here.  \n\nThe listening post is the opposite kind of dangerous. No crowds, no glow, just vacuum-thin air and rows of redacted reports where careers came to die. Whatever ledger they kept off the record linked his tampered departures to official silence, and that makes it one of the last honest mirrors left. If I dig there, I am reaching for names, ships, and coordinates the bureaus decided not to remember, the kind of proof that turns a ghost story into something the UC and Freestar can no longer ignore.
zh:
霓虹城的屋顶是个无法清醒思考的地方。电网中每一道弧光、每一个把飞船朝同一方向轻推的被遗忘的着陆脉冲，都像站在他做梦时的颅骨里。
如果我顺着那条线追，我就是在赌这座城市的旧习惯与他新的编辑如今是同一样东西，赌沃利上空的脉动是他最爱逃亡路线的心跳。
这是裹在噪声与企业阴影里的风险，但如果他还在任何地方调校天空，那就是这里。

监听站是另一种危险。没有人群、没有辉光，只有稀薄如真空的空气，以及一排排职业在此终结的涂黑报告。
无论他们私下保留了什么账册，它都把他被篡改的离港记录与官方的沉默连在一起，这使它成为仅存的几面诚实镜子之一。
如果我在那里挖掘，我就是在伸手去够那些各局决定不再记住的名字、船只与坐标——那种能把幽灵故事变成联殖与星联再也无法忽视之物的证据。

#en: Ryujin's tower is the loud path. Bright lights, security badges, and executives who pretend they do not recognize the name on my lips. If I dig there, I am cutting into live flesh corporate shipping, black clinic runs, grav spikes smoothed out of the ledgers by very expensive hands. High risk, higher leverage. If I can pry loose the routes they are hiding, I will not just know where he went next, I will know who paid to look the other way. That kind of knowledge spends well, if it does not get me spaced first.\n\nThe relay bunker is the quiet path. Dust, dead terminals, and one forgotten grid still whispering to itself. No polished lies there, just raw patrol data and a string of anomalies that look more and more like a single pilot threading the same forbidden band of sky. Less noise, more time alone with whatever those readings really mean. If there is a pattern he did not intend anyone to see, it will be entombed in those racks, waiting for the first fool stubborn enough to wake it.
zh:
龙神大厦是响亮的路。明亮的灯光、安保徽章，以及那些假装不认识我口中那名字的高管。
如果我在那里挖掘，我就是在切开活肉：企业航运、黑诊所航线、被极其昂贵的手从账册里抹平的重力尖峰。高风险、更高筹码。
如果我能撬出他们藏着的航线，我不仅会知道他下一步去了哪里，还会知道是谁出钱让他们别过头去。
这种知识很值钱——只要它没先把我送进太空。

中继碉堡是安静的路。尘土、死去的终端，以及一张仍在对自己低语的被遗忘电网。
那里没有光鲜的谎言，只有生的巡逻数据，以及一串越来越像某位飞行员穿引同一条禁空带的异常。
噪声更少，有更多时间独处，去弄懂那些读数究竟意味着什么。如果他有一个不打算被任何人看见的图案，它就会葬身在那几排架子里，等着第一个固执到愿意唤醒它的傻子。

#en: The cavern lead is dirt under the fingernails, close-range and personal. Smugglers, nervous quartermasters, favors logged in grease and half-truths. If I push there, I am leaning into the human side of her web: the people she pays, the captains who owe her their hides, the off-the-books haulers who know exactly which wrecks she is bleeding. Messy and loud, but names, faces, and grudges have a way of slipping when someone with a gun is listening.  \n\nThe orbital lead is colder, cleaner, more like her. That listening post in deep shadow is where the math lives: unmarked relays, bent shipping lanes, a diagram of every graveyard she has been secretly stitching together. If I take that route, I am chasing her mind instead of her clients, pulling on the thread that ties the gas giant, the derelicts, and that hidden barge into one shape. Fewer witnesses, more risk, but if I want to see the whole design instead of just the blood it spills, that is where the sky itself is starting to look wrong.
zh:
洞穴那条线索是沾在指甲缝里的泥，近距离且针对个人。走私贩、紧张的军需官、记在油污与半真半假里的人情。
如果我朝那里施压，我就是在靠向她那张网的人情一面：她付钱的人、欠她性命的人、清楚知道她在给哪些残骸放血的账外运货船员。
混乱而嘈杂，但当有个带着枪的人在听时，名字、面孔与积怨总会泄露。

轨道那条线索更冷、更干净，更像她。深影里的那座监听站是数学所在之处：未标记的中继站、弯曲的航运航道，一张她一直在秘密缝合的每一座墓场的图解。
如果我走那条路，我追的是她的头脑而非她的客户，拉扯那根把气态巨行星、废弃船与那艘隐秘驳船系成一体的线。
目击者更少、风险更大，但如果我想看到整个设计而非它洒出的鲜血，那就是天空本身开始显得不对劲的地方。

#en: The station is the clean choice on paper. Bright halls, respectable badges, the illusion that if I just pull the right file, everything will line up into something resembling the truth. Dig there and I am tangling with administrators, researchers, and boardroom ghosts who turned her improvisations into product lines. It is the path where ink and signatures matter, where Catalyst is either a scapegoat or an uncredited architect of half their breakthroughs.\n\nThe listening post is the dirty choice, all dust and dead channels and the Renegade Guard cutting out whatever does not fit their version of events. Going there means stepping into the crosshairs of people who know exactly how command erases problems, because they used to be the eraser. If I want the story that never made it into any archive the names, the coordinates, the casualties that did not officially exist I will have to walk through a nest of ex-soldiers who already decided the truth is more dangerous than any chem she ever mixed.
zh:
那座空间站是纸面上的干净选择。明亮的大厅、体面的徽章，以及一种幻觉：只要我调出正确的档案，一切就会排列成某种接近真相的东西。
在那里挖掘，我就要与行政人员、研究员，以及那些把她的临场发挥变成产品线的董事会幽灵纠缠。
那是一条墨水与签名说了算的路，在那里"催化剂"要么是替罪羊，要么是他们半数突破的无名建筑师。

监听站是肮脏的选择，满是尘土与死去的频道，还有"叛卫"在剪掉任何不符合他们版本事件的东西。
去那里意味着踏进那些清楚知道指挥部如何抹除麻烦的人的准星——因为他们过去就是那把橡皮擦。
如果我想要那个从未进入任何档案的故事——那些名字、坐标，那些官方上并不存在的伤亡——我就得穿过一窝已经认定真相比她调过的任何药剂都危险的老兵。

#en: The lab trail is tempting. Quiet corridors, dormant diagnostics, all the ghosts of "official" science humming just loud enough to mask what he slipped in underneath. If I dig through those dead displays, I might finally see his work in its raw form, before pirates, corporates, and UC cut-outs started passing it around as campfire myth. Cleaner data, less incoming fire. More time to think about whether he is seeing monsters in the static, or whether everyone else is just pretending not to hear them.\n\nThe cache in the busy lane is different. That is where theory turns into wreckage and near-misses, where his numbers actually shove metal and lives off their plotted courses. Cracking open something he trusted enough to leave under constant traffic will show exactly which routes he is steering toward the dark, and who he is protecting or condemning in the process. Dirtier work, more guns pointed my way, but the pattern would not be abstract anymore; it would have names, schedules, and a heading.
zh:
实验室那条线索很诱人。安静的走廊、休眠的诊断设备，所有"官方"科学的幽灵都在嗡鸣，声音刚好足以掩盖他在底下塞进的东西。
如果我翻掘那些死去的显示屏，也许终于能看到他工作的原始形态——在海盗、企业与联殖的中间人开始把它当作篝火神话传播之前。
数据更干净，来袭火力更少。也有更多时间去想：究竟是他在静电里看见了怪物，还是别人都只是假装没听见它们。

繁忙航道里的藏匿点则不同。那是理论变成残骸与惊险接近的地方，是他的数字真正把金属与性命推离既定航线的所在。
撬开某件他信任到敢留在持续交通之下的东西，就会准确显示他正把哪些航线引向黑暗，以及在此过程中他在保护或判罪谁。
更肮脏的工作，更多枪口指向我，但图案将不再抽象；它会有名字、时刻表和航向。

#en: Neon keeps coming up in the traffic, a smear of dirty signal under the Span where every secret eventually gets traded for credits or leverage. If I drop back into that underbelly, I am walking into a maze of fixers, smugglers, and corporate cleaners who all swear they only heard the story secondhand. High risk, but if I can pry loose the piece that started on that dead Navy hull and rode the static rimward, it might tell me who has been buying silence on an industrial scale.  \n\nThe relay shack is the opposite problem. No crowds, no witnesses, just old hardware and lazier sins. Those duplicated routes and altered bands did not park there by accident; someone bet that nobody audits a forgotten node as long as the smuggling runs stay quiet. Safer to reach, maybe, but quieter does not mean harmless. If the cached fragments really line up with clinic payouts and burned farms, then that rock is not just dead weight in space. It is where the pattern finally stops being rumor and starts naming names.
zh:
霓虹城在交通中一再出现，是跨桥之下一抹肮脏的信号，在那里每个秘密最终都会被换成信用或筹码。
如果我重新落回那片下层，我就走进了调停人、走私贩与企业清道夫构成的迷宫——他们全都发誓自己只是二手听来的故事。
高风险，但如果我能撬出那块始于那具死海军船体、并骑着静电向外缘漂去的东西，它也许能告诉我谁一直在以工业规模收买沉默。

那座中继小屋是相反的问题。没有人群、没有目击者，只有旧硬件与更懒散的罪。
那些重复的航线与被篡改的频带不是偶然停在那里的；有人赌定只要走私航次保持安静，就没人会去审计一座被遗忘的节点。
到达也许更安全，但更安静并不意味着无害。如果缓存的碎片真的与诊所付款和焚毁的农场对得上，那么那块岩石就不只是太空中的死重。它是图案终于不再是传言、而开始点出名字的地方。

#en: The forgotten base has a certain logic to it. Old concrete, dead arrays, the kind of place bureaucracies misplace in their own archives. If those encoded routes really thread the gaps between LIST scans and Argos lanes, then cracking them turns the chase from a galaxy-wide search into a few narrow corridors. Scrapstar Haulers sniffing around means the stories have value, but not enough for anyone to file a report. Following this lead is betting that his genius lives in the way he moves, not in where he trades.\n\nThe buoy in quiet drift is a different kind of temptation. Harvest models, redlined and quietly overwritten, would show every world he has poisoned with false promise and every neglected corridor he trusted to slip away afterward. That clue has been hanging in the dark long enough for patrols and smugglers alike to forget it exists, which feels exactly like his style. Chasing this thread means learning which colonies he chose to wound, and maybe why he thinks the numbers justify the bodies.
zh:
这座被遗忘的基地自有其逻辑。旧混凝土、死去的阵列，那种官僚机构会在自家档案里放错地方的地方。
如果那些编码航线真的穿在独立盟扫描与阿戈斯航道的空隙之间，那么破解它们就能把追查从一场全星系搜索变成少数几条狭窄走廊。
废星运货队在附近嗅探，意味着这些故事有价值，但还不值得任何人提交报告。
顺着这条线索，就是在赌他的天才活在他行动的方式里，而非他交易的地点中。

安静漂移中的那座浮标是另一种诱惑。被标红并悄然覆盖的收获模型，会显示出他用虚假承诺毒害过的每一颗世界，以及他信赖着事后能溜走的每一条被忽视走廊。
那条线索在黑暗中挂了足够久，久到巡逻队与走私贩都忘了它存在，这感觉正是他的风格。
追这条线意味着弄清他选择伤害哪些殖民地，也许还有他为什么认为数字能为尸体开脱。

#en: Gagarin Landing is dirty, loud, and honest about it. Down in the backlines where the pipes sweat and the catwalks rust, somebody helped him bend the freight stream toward the graveyard and then never came back to seal their work. If I dig through those splice points, I might find a name, a face, maybe even the one person he trusted enough to share his route with. Exposing his partner would crack open his support network and give me leverage that steel and bullets cannot.\n\nThe orbital node is colder, cleaner, and a lot less forgiving. No witnesses there, just telemetry and the ghosts of bad decisions: half fixed coordinates, aborted burns, tug signatures nudged a few degrees off regulation. If I tap that buffer before SysDef or some corporate auditor wipes it, I should pull a pure pattern of his jumps a mathematically precise arc toward the dead space he keeps circling. That route would not just point at where he hides; it would prove how long he has been doing it while everyone else pretended not to see.
zh:
加加林着陆点肮脏、吵闹，而且对此很诚实。在管道渗水、栈桥生锈的后线区域，有人帮他把货流弯向墓场，然后再没回来封住自己的工程。
如果我翻掘那些接驳点，也许能找到一个名字、一张面孔，也许甚至是他信任到愿意分享航线的唯一那个人。
揭出他的伙伴，就能撬开他的支持网络，给我钢铁与子弹给不了的筹码。

轨道节点更冷、更干净，也远不容情。那里没有目击者，只有遥测与糟糕决策的幽灵：半被修正的坐标、中断的点火、被推离规程几度的拖船特征。
如果我在联殖防务或某位企业审计员擦掉它之前接入那块缓冲区，我应该能取出一道纯粹的他跃迁图案——一条精确朝向他不停止环绕的死寂空域的数学弧线。
那条路线不仅会指出他藏在哪；它会证明他这么做已经多久，而别人都假装没看见。

#en: Ryujin's tower looks clean from the outside, all glass and lightning and smiling reception kiosks, but the real weather is in whatever they bury under access levels and nondisclosure clauses. The idea of paging through their vent schedules and scrubber diagnostics is tempting; if he has friends in high places, they will have left fingerprints in the airflow. It is the softer play, on paper, but prying truth out of a corporation that profits from silence can be more dangerous than trading fire with pirates.\n\nThe other path runs colder, through tracking beacons and engine residue hanging in orbit over half-starved worlds. The drift data does not flinch the way people do, and the same masked shuttle trail keeps looping past every quiet failure I have visited since that first forgotten outpost and the courier that never made its delivery. If I follow the pattern through open space instead of corporate corridors, I might finally see where his route bends next, before another sky changes color without warning.
zh:
龙神大厦从外面看很干净，满是玻璃、闪电与微笑的接待亭，但真正的天气藏在他们埋在权限等级与保密条款之下的东西里。
翻阅他们的通风时刻表与净化器诊断很有诱惑力；如果他在高层有朋友，他们会在气流里留下指纹。
纸面上这是更温和的一着，但从一家靠沉默牟利的企业嘴里撬出真相，可能比与海盗交火更危险。

另一条路更冷，穿过悬在半饥饿世界上方的追踪信标与引擎残留。
漂移数据不会像人那样畏惧退缩，而同一道被遮蔽的穿梭机痕迹，不断绕经我自第一座被遗忘哨站和那艘从未完成投递的信使飞船以来造访的每一处安静失败。
如果我沿着这个图案穿过开阔太空而非企业走廊，也许终于能看到他的航线下一步在何处弯折——赶在又一片天空毫无预警地变色之前。

#en: The tower is the dirty, civilized choice. Climate control, keycards, guards who still think orders mean something, and somewhere in all that glass and steel, the paper trail that says who paid for the experiments and who cleaned the results. If I walk into that place and shake the right files loose, I might finally see the signatures behind the anomalies instead of just their aftermath. But that also means putting my face and biometrics in the same building as the people who still pretend this is all just "variance."\n\nThe lonely orbit is the honest kind of danger. No politics, no briefing rooms, just an off-lane node quietly bending jump math until ships and lives fall where someone wants them. If I can get close enough to listen, I might catch the raw routing changes before they get laundered through a dozen systems. Of course, whoever set that anchor will have expected someone like me to come sniffing around, and out there there is nothing between us but vacuum and whatever traps they left in the dark.
zh:
塔是肮脏而文明的选择。气候控制、门禁卡、那些仍以为命令有意义的守卫，而在那片玻璃与钢铁之中某处，有一条纸面线索，写明谁为实验付了钱、谁清理了结果。
如果我走进那地方、抖出正确的档案，也许终于能看到异常背后的签名，而不只是它们的后果。
但那也意味着把我的面孔与生物特征，与那些仍假装这一切只是"偏差"的人放进同一栋楼里。

那片孤独的轨道是诚实的那种危险。没有政治、没有简报室，只有一座账外节点在悄悄弯折跃迁数学，直到飞船与性命落向某人想要它们落的地方。
如果我能靠得够近去倾听，也许能在那些原始航路改动被十几个系统洗白之前抓住它们。
当然，布下那个锚点的人一定料到会有我这样的人来嗅探，而在那里，我们之间只有真空，以及他们留在黑暗中的陷阱。

#en: The underbelly routes are closer, and they feel like her handwriting. Someone took a mess of stolen conduits and lazy access control and turned it into geometry, a clean set of paths only an ex-inspector would trust. If I walk those tunnels, I am walking in step with her habits, seeing which junctions she marked as safe and which ones she left to burn. It is personal, almost intimate, which makes it the smarter choice if I want to understand the mind that keeps breaking ships without ever firing a shot.\n\nThe salvage pit is uglier, louder, and a long way from subtle. Rust, gossip, and half-melted hardware, all stacked in a trench nobody sane bothers to audit. But a fragment of a flight path thrown away there says she is confident, maybe even careless, and that kind of arrogance leaves sharper footprints. If I chase that datapack, I am betting on hard numbers over instinct, trusting that the pattern of bad jumps and erased annexes will finally spell out where she is heading instead of just where she has already been.
zh:
下层路线更近，而且它们像她的笔迹。
有人把一堆偷来的导管与松懈的门禁变成几何，一套只有前检查员才会信任的干净路径。
如果我走过那些隧道，我就是在与她的习惯同步行进，看到她标为安全的节点，以及她任由烧毁的节点。
这是私人的、近乎亲密的，这使它成为更聪明的选择——如果我想理解那个从不发一枪就不断弄坏飞船的头脑。

打捞坑更丑陋、更吵闹，离"精妙"很远。锈、闲话与半熔的硬件堆在一条没有理智人会费心审计的沟里。
但一段被丢在那里的飞行路径碎片说明她自信，甚至可能粗心，而这种傲慢会留下更锋利的足迹。
如果我追那个数据包，我就是在拿硬数据赌过直觉，相信那些糟糕跃迁与被抹除附属区的图案，终于能拼出她正前往何处，而不只是她已去过何处。

#en: Neon's underbelly is all breath and rumor. Down there, her work is etched in handshakes and half-paid favors, not numbers. If I go back into that maze of leaking pipes and humming grid-lines, I will be bartering for stories, trying to stitch together a pattern from dockhands who are more afraid of losing their next payout than losing their memories. Risk is high, payoff intangible: a better sense of how she thinks, where she feels safe, who she trusts when everything goes loud.\n\nThe moonside relay is colder. Metal, manifests, and one broker who has already proven he files sins under "miscellaneous cargo." On that station, her shadow turns into timestamps and repeat receiver tags, proof that someone has been laundering entire routes around official lanes for years. Fewer people to work through, but the ones there will have friends in Trade Authority and worse. If I want to pin her to a specific jump, this is where the trail hardens into something I can hold up in a rival's face and say: you have been helping a ghost.
zh:
霓虹城的下层全是气息与传言。在那里，她的作品刻在握手与半付的人情上，而非数字里。
如果我回到那个漏水管与嗡鸣电网构成的迷宫里，我就要用故事换取故事，试图从那些害怕失去下一笔报酬甚于失去记忆的码头工人口中缝出一个图案。
风险高，回报无形：更清楚地感受她如何思考、在何处感到安全、当一切喧嚣时她信任谁。

月球侧的中继站更冷。金属、舱单，以及一名已经证明自己会把罪行归入"杂项货物"的经纪商。
在那座空间站上，她的影子变成时间戳与重复的接收器标签，证明有人多年来一直绕着官方航道洗白整条路线。
要打交道的人更少，但那里的人会有贸易管理局乃至更糟的朋友。
如果我想把她钉在某一次具体的跃迁上，那就是线索硬化成我能举到对手脸上说"你一直在帮一个幽灵"的东西的地方。

#en: Neon's lower decks have a way of stripping the varnish off a story. In the underbelly, people move code like contraband, and nobody asks where the climate models came from as long as the credits clear. If he ever sold his tricks to keep himself afloat, this is where the buyers would be. Following that thread means leaning on smugglers and data-brokers, wading through Aurora haze and backroom favors, hoping one of them slips and admits who has been feeding them storm maps that do not match the sky.\n\nThe research module is different. Cold, quiet, almost honest by comparison. This is where the first mistake happened, before the lies were packaged and resold in places like Neon. Someone rerouted a harmless telemetry feed and turned a forgotten node into a hinge for re-writing navigation. If I chase that path, I am gambling that the original exploit still holds his signature, buried under half-scrubbed logs and abandoned experiments. Less noise, fewer guns, more time alone with whatever pattern he thought nobody would ever notice.
zh:
霓虹城的下层甲板有一种把故事打磨掉光漆的本事。在下层，人们像搬违禁品一样搬运代码，只要信用到账，没人问气候模型是从哪来的。
如果他为了维持自己而出卖过把戏，买家就在这里。
顺着那条线，就意味着倚靠走私贩与数据经纪商，蹚过极光的迷雾与密室人情，指望他们中有人失口承认是谁一直在给他们喂与天空不符的风暴图。

研究模块则不同。寒冷、安静，相比之下几乎算诚实。
最初的错误就发生在这里——在谎言被包装并在霓虹城这样的地方转售之前。有人改道了一条无害的遥测馈送，把一座被遗忘的节点变成重写导航的铰链。
如果我追那条路，我就是在赌最初的漏洞仍带着他的特征，埋在半被擦净的日志与被弃实验之下。噪声更少、枪更少，有更多时间独处，陪着那个他以为没人会注意到的图案。

#en: Ryujin's tower is the civilized option, at least on paper. Climate control, polished stone, security that smiles while it sizes you for a body bag. If they really bought a copy of those old conditioning trees, the answers are in a boardroom vault or buried three layers deep in their black R&D. Cutting in there means sifting half-truths from executives who lie for a living and systems designed to erase their own footprints. High risk, but if I find the right shard, I might finally see who has been holding his leash.\n\nOut in the empty lanes, the only witnesses are dead transponders and whatever is still riding that orbital curve. The signal is messy, stitched across old battles and forgotten evac routes, but it feels closer to his real trail than any corporate ledger. Track it, and I am following the same invisible orders he has been obeying since the garrison burned. Fewer locked doors, more guns pointed at my hull, and a greater chance that the next piece in the chain is not a file at all, but a patient he never finished with.
zh:
龙神大厦是文明的选项，至少纸面上如此。气候控制、打磨过的石头、一边微笑一边为你量裹尸袋尺寸的安保。
如果他们真的买下那些旧条件化模型树的一份副本，答案就在某间董事会的保险库里，或深埋在他们黑色研发的三层之下。
切入那里意味着从靠说谎为生的高管、以及被设计来抹去自身足迹的系统里筛出半真半假。
高风险，但如果我找对那块碎片，也许终于能看到是谁一直牵着他的皮带。

在空荡的航道中，唯一的目击者是死去的应答器，以及仍在骑乘那道轨道曲线的什么东西。
信号混乱，缝合着旧战役与被遗忘的撤离路线，但它感觉比任何企业账册都更贴近他真正的踪迹。
追踪它，我就在遵循自驻军焚毁以来他一直服从的同一批看不见的命令。锁门更少，指向我船体的枪更多，而链条中下一环根本不是文件、而是他从未处理完的某个病人的可能也更大。

#en: Down in Neon's underbelly, the pattern smells like money and blood. Captains taking the same crooked slice of sky, medics treating burns that look more like field shear than gunfire, brokers suddenly trading in old patrol data. If I lean into this, I am stepping into a marketplace of secrets, where every answer has a price and Ryujin ears are never far away. It is messy, dangerous, crowded with other people's sins but it might show me who has been paying to keep those anomalies misfiled as malfunctions.\n\nThe farm ring angle is quieter, more mechanical, almost honest on the surface. A forgotten food rig turned permanent, its plumbing altered by someone who thinks in flow rates and vector diagrams, not bribes. Following that lead means crawling through an old ship's bones, tracing which "temporary" feeds were left drawing power and why a grow rack needs its own dedicated jump calibration. It is slower work, more solitude, fewer guns in my face but if he built a habit of hiding inside stopped gap fixes, this is where his hand will be clearest.
zh:
在霓虹城的下层，这个图案闻起来像钱与血。船长们选取天空中同样扭曲的一角，医者治疗那些更像场域剪切而非枪伤造成的灼伤，经纪商突然开始交易旧的巡逻数据。
如果我深入进去，我就踏进了一个秘密集市，那里每个答案都有价格，而龙神的耳朵从不遥远。
它混乱、危险，挤满别人的罪孽，但它也许能让我看到谁一直在出钱把那些异常错误归档成"故障"。

农场环那条角度更安静、更机械，表面上几乎诚实。
一座被遗忘的食物钻井被改为永久设施，它的管路被一个以流量与矢量图、而非贿赂来思考的人改过。
顺着那条线索，意味着在一艘旧船骨架里爬行，追查哪些"临时"馈送被留着供电、以及为何一个种植架需要它自己专属的跃迁校准。
这是更慢的工作、更多独处、更少枪口对着我的脸，但如果他养成了藏在停滞的间隙修补里的习惯，这里就是他的手最清晰的地方。

#en: The dead robotics lab feels like the place where this all began to spin out of control, where theory first brushed against hardware and left scorch marks behind. If I go back there and dig deeper, I am chasing origins: early grav tweaks, half-scrubbed simulations, the first proof that someone was willing to bend climate and jump geometry in the same breath. It is slower, dirtier work, and I will have to peel information out from under scavengers who do not even know what they are sitting on, but it might tell me why he chose this path.\n\nThe orbital beacon is different. That node sits where his work is alive, not historical, quietly shaving angles off flight paths while the rest of the system pretends nothing is wrong. If I follow that route, I am stepping straight into his current, watching the sky distort in real time. The risk is higher: whatever defenses he has left will be tied to those calibration streams, and if I misstep, I will announce myself to the same unseen hand that has been moving storms and satellites like pieces on a board.
zh:
那座废弃机器人实验室感觉像是这一切开始失控的地方，理论第一次擦过硬件并留下焦痕之处。
如果我回到那里挖得更深，我追的是起源：早期的重力微调、半被擦净的模拟，以及有人愿意在同一口气里弯折气候与跃迁几何的第一份证据。
这是更慢、更脏的工作，我将不得不从那些甚至不知道自己坐在什么上面的拾荒者底下剥出信息，但它也许能告诉我他为什么选择这条路。

轨道信标则不同。那座节点所在之处，他的工作是活的，而非历史的，它悄悄从飞行路径上削去角度，而星系其余部分假装一切正常。
如果我顺着那条路线，我就径直踏进他的水流，实时看着天空扭曲。
风险更高：他留下的无论是什么防御都会与那些校准流绑定，而如果我踩错一步，我就会向那只一直在把风暴与卫星当作棋盘棋子挪动的看不见的手宣告自己的存在。

#en: Gagarin Landing is the straightest line: heavy industry, corporate refurb work, and a whole lot of numbers that do not quite match the hulls they are attached to. If there is a technical trick behind her disappearing act, it is probably buried there under legitimate work orders and "harmless" corrections. Walking into that mess means wading through company handlers and nervous techs who know how fragile their livelihoods are. High risk, but if I want the engineering blueprint of her lane, that is where the systems speak.\n\nThe moonside relay is thinner air in every sense. A handful of patched habitats, a nervous broker, and a culture built on pretending the cargo never existed in the first place. No auditors, no inspectors, just people who live off gaps in the record. The story there will be rumor, coded manifests, and the human side of her network: who she pays, who she spares, who she lets starve. Less metal, more lies. If I want to understand why so many captains still whisper her name like a warning instead of a curse, that is where I listen.
zh:
加加林着陆点是最直的一条线：重工业、企业翻新工程，以及一大堆与其所附船体并不完全吻合的数字。
如果她消失的把戏背后有技术诀窍，它多半埋在那里，藏在合法工单与"无害"修正之下。
走进那团混乱，意味着蹚过企业管事与神经紧张、深知自己生计多么脆弱的技师。
高风险，但如果我想要她那航道的工程蓝图，那就是系统说话的地方。

月球侧的中继站在每种意义上空气都更稀薄。几处打过补丁的居所、一名紧张的经纪商，以及一种建立在假装货物从一开始就不存在的文化。
没有审计员、没有检查员，只有靠记录缺口过活的人。
那里的故事将是传言、编码的舱单，以及她网络的人情面：她付钱给谁、她放过谁、她任谁挨饿。金属更少，谎言更多。
如果我想理解为什么这么多船长的低声念她的名字像念一句警告而非诅咒，那就是我倾听的地方。

#en: Ryujin's tower would be the tidy cut. Climate control, polished stone, security guards who pretend they do not see what their employers pay to hide. If I go there, I am not just chasing a rogue navigator, I am kicking the legs out from under whatever board signed off on these experiments. Paper trails, scrubbed payouts, research budgets rewritten into alibis. It is cleaner work, at least on the surface, but stepping into that building means treating this like a crime of suits, not just one woman weaponizing math.\n\nThe listening post is the opposite end of the spectrum raw sky, dead hardware, mercs instead of receptionists. Hotel Hardstrike holding the line over repurposed UC ears, guarding beacon logs no one wants to admit still exist. If I go there first, I am betting that the truth is buried in noise and old war habits, not balance sheets. More guns, fewer lawyers. One path puts me in boardrooms and back channels, the other drops me in a forgotten bunker with mercenaries paid to ask no questions. Either way, the same signature keeps surfacing in the data.
zh:
龙神大厦会是干净利落的一刀。气候控制、打磨过的石头、假装看不见雇主花钱掩埋什么的保安。
如果我去那里，我追的不只是一名失控的领航员，我是在把任何为这些实验签字的董事会桌子下的腿踢断。
纸面线索、被擦净的付款、被改写成托词的研究预算。
这是更干净的工作，至少表面上，但踏进那栋楼意味着把这当作一桩由西装犯下的罪，而非只是一个女人把数学武器化。

监听站在光谱的另一端：生的天空、死去的硬件，雇来的枪手而非接待员。
"硬击旅"守着被改用的联殖耳朵，守护着没人愿意承认仍然存在的信标日志。
如果我先去那里，我就是在赌真相埋在噪声与旧战争习惯里，而非资产负债表里。枪更多，律师更少。
一条路把我带进董事会与后门渠道，另一条把我丢进一座被遗忘的碉堡，去面对被收买来不问问题的雇佣兵。无论哪条，同一个特征都在数据中不断浮现。

#en: If I head for the Clinic, I go where the damage is catalogued and given names. Every grav-burned pilot, every fractured mind from a bad jump, all quietly stored behind polite smiles and redacted reports. If his work ever brushed flesh, it is written there in nerve maps and scar tissue. The risk is eyes on me from every authority that cares about their reputation, but the payoff is simple and sharp: I might finally see what his numbers do to real people instead of empty hulls.\n\nIf I drop to the old recon hide, I am chasing the first honest look at how he slips through a net designed to catch everything. The bunker is dead on paper, but its recorders were built to watch without blinking, and they do not care whose career gets ruined by what they saw. Less politics, more ghosts: cold air, old UC hardware, and maybe one uncut sequence of a ship walking between sensor sweeps like it knows where the blind spots live. One path walks me into crowded corridors and whispered testimonies; the other into dust, silence, and raw telemetry. Either way, his shadow is waiting.
zh:
如果我前往星际诊所号，我就是去那些伤害被编目并赋予名字的地方。
每一个被重力灼伤的飞行员、每一个因糟糕跃迁而破碎的心智，都被安静地收在礼貌的微笑与涂黑的报告之后。
如果他的工作曾擦过血肉，它就写在那里的神经图谱与疤痕组织里。
风险是每个在乎自身声誉的当局都会盯着我，但回报简单而锋利：我也许终于能看到他的数字对真实的人、而非空荡船体做了什么。

如果我下到那座旧侦察隐蔽点，我追的是第一次诚实地看清他如何溜过一张被设计来捕捉一切的大网。
那座碉堡在纸面上已死，但它的记录仪被造来不眨眼地注视，而它们不在乎谁的前程会被它们所见之物毁掉。
政治更少，幽灵更多：冰冷的空气、旧联殖硬件，也许还有一段未被剪切的连续影像——一艘飞船在传感器扫描之间穿行，仿佛知道盲点住在哪里。
一条路把我带进拥挤的走廊与低语的证词；另一条带进尘土、寂静与原始遥测。无论哪条，他的影子都在等着。

#en: Neon's skyline is a liar's chorus, but the rooftops hum with the truth underneath it. Up there, routes are sold between drinks, fees are laundered through private pads, and people talk more freely when they think the wind will carry their secrets away. If Vector ever bragged, even by accident, it was probably in the shadow of the Span, his coordinates traded like ghost stories between smugglers and corporate fixers. Chasing that thread means wading into gossip, greasing palms, and listening hard for one voice that talks in numbers instead of names.\n\nThe relay bunker is different. No noise, no drinks, just machines that never learned how to lie. Someone pulled atmospheric traces there and saw something they should not have, then quietly stepped off the grid. The logs they left behind read the same way every time: the same anomaly, the same path through restricted sky. Following that line means trusting cold data over street talk, digging into whatever is riding inside that forgotten SysDef hull and hoping the people who were supposed to clean this up are not still watching.
zh:
霓虹城的天际线是一个说谎者的合唱，但屋顶嗡嗡作响着它底下的真相。
在上面，航线在酒桌之间被出售，费用通过私人停机坪洗白，而人们在以为风会把秘密带走时说得更放开。
如果"向量"曾吹嘘过，哪怕是无意的，那多半就在跨桥的阴影里，他的坐标像幽灵故事一样在走私贩与企业调停人之间被交易。
追这条线意味着蹚进闲话、给人塞钱，并努力倾听一个用数字而非名字说话的声音。

中继碉堡则不同。没有噪声、没有酒，只有从未学会如何说谎的机器。
有人在那里提取过大气痕迹，看见了不该看见的东西，随后悄然脱离网络。
他们留下的日志每次读起来都一样：同样的异常，同样穿过受限天空的路径。
顺着那条线，意味着信任冷数据胜过街头闲谈，挖进那具被遗忘联殖防务船体里骑乘着什么，并指望那些本该清理此事的人没有还在盯着。

#en: The Underbelly trail feels like chasing whispers through a power grid. If Vector is bleeding off city juice to push those impossible jumps, somebody down there has seen the lights flicker at the wrong time. It will mean leaning on coil crews and Ghost Coil hangers-on, parsing shrugs and half-finished sentences until a pattern finally shakes loose. Low light, close quarters, every conversation a chance to step on Ryujin toes or some local gang's territory, but if I crack their work logs I might see when and where his ship plugs into Neon's heartbeat.\n\nThe wreck in orbit is colder, simpler, and maybe more honest. Steel remembers what people would rather argue about, and those scorched plates are a flight recorder carved in metal. Follow the twist in the struts, map the angle of that sideways burn, and I could pin down the corridor he is been rehearsing, the direction he keeps trying to tear open. It is riskier in different ways: dead space, thin cover, and anyone else hunting these ghost jumps might be watching the same drifting grave, waiting to see who comes to read its scars.
zh:
下层那条线索感觉像在电网里追逐低语。
如果"向量"在从城市偷电来推动那些不可能完成的跃迁，下面一定有人见过灯在错误的时刻闪烁。
这将意味着倚靠线圈班组与幽灵线圈的附庸，解析耸肩与半截句子，直到一个图案终于抖落出来。
光线昏暗、空间逼仄，每一次交谈都可能踩到龙神的脚趾或某个本地帮派的地盘，但如果我破解他们的工作日志，也许能看出他的飞船在何时何地接入霓虹城的心跳。

轨道上的残骸更冷、更简单，也许更诚实。钢铁会记住人们宁愿争辩的东西，而那些烧焦的钢板就是一枚以金属刻成的飞行记录仪。
顺着支杆的扭曲追下去，把那道侧向燃烧的角度标出来，我也许能钉死他一直在演练的走廊、他不断试图撕开的方向。
它在不同的意义上更冒险：死寂的空间、稀薄的掩体，而其他任何在狩猎这些幽灵跃迁的人，也许正盯着同一座漂流的坟墓，等着看谁来读取它的伤疤。

#en: Gagarin is the safer kind of rotten. Paper trails, nervous clerks, off-world suits pretending not to see the dust caking their server racks. If she sold the sky to anyone, the proof is probably humming away in those annex stacks, buried under invoices and falsified maintenance reports. Walking in means talking to people, peeling back corporate lies one spreadsheet at a time, maybe finding out who paid her and why they needed the storms moved. It feels like the path to answers that end up in a tribunal, not a morgue.\n\nThat wreck out in the orbital junk-ring is another story. No witnesses, no politics, just scorched metal quietly stitching together every odd reading I have chased so far. If that telemetry really is the hinge in her pattern, cracking it open might finally show where all these altered skies converge next. But the kind of people who use dead satellites as waypoints do not like being seen, and if she has built herself a back door through obsolete UC hardware, following it means stepping into a place she has been shaping, pressure line by pressure line, for a very long time.
zh:
加加林星是更安全的那种腐坏。纸面线索、神经紧张的文书、假装看不见服务器架上积尘的外派西装们。
如果她把天空卖给了谁，证据多半在那些附属区的架列里嗡鸣，埋在发票与伪造的维护报告之下。
走进去意味着与人交谈，一张电子表格一张电子表格地剥开企业的谎言，也许能弄清是谁付钱给她、以及他们为什么需要那些风暴被挪动。
它感觉像通往那种最终出现在法庭、而非停尸房的答案的路。

轨道废料环里的那具残骸则是另一回事。没有目击者、没有政治，只有烧焦的金属，在悄然把我迄今追查的每一处古怪读数缝在一起。
如果那道遥测真是她图案中的铰链，撬开它也许终于能显示这些被篡改的天空接下来都汇聚到何处。
但那种把死卫星当作航点的人不喜欢被看见，而如果她为自己造了一扇穿过过时联殖硬件的后门，顺着它就意味着踏进一个她一直在塑造的地方——一条压力线接一条压力线，塑了非常久。

#en: The Well is close, crowded, and loud enough to hide the kind of questions I need to ask. Down there, the stories come wrapped in debt and old favors; people talk because they owe someone, or because they hate someone more than they fear MacLeod. If his name is written anywhere official, it is in the gaps between payments, the mismatched cargo tallies, the shifts nobody wants to remember working. Stepping into that maze means dealing with dockside politics and quiet threats, but the payoff could be the whole network laid bare on a single, dirty backroom slate.\n\nThe moonside relay is colder in every sense. Fewer eyes, longer shadows, and a broker who already flinched when my last questions grazed the truth. Out there, the noise is lower and the lies are easier to isolate against the hum of the reactor. The manifests running through that place are already too neat, too rehearsed; if I press hard enough, something will crack, and the spine of this smuggling line might light up clear as a navigation grid. Higher risk if the broker decides to warn him, but cleaner, sharper answers if he does not.
zh:
深井区很近、拥挤，而且吵闹得足以掩盖我需要问的那类问题。
在那里，故事裹在债务与旧人情里；人们开口是因为他们欠某人什么，或是因为他们恨某人甚于怕麦克劳德。
如果他的名字写在任何官方文件上，那就是在付款之间的空隙里、对不上的货物清单里、没人愿意记得自己上过的班次里。
踏进那座迷宫意味着应付码头政治与无声的威胁，但回报可能是整张网络在一件肮脏的后室石板上被彻底摊开。

月球侧的中继站在每种意义上都更冷。眼睛更少、影子更长，还有一名在我上次的问题擦到真相时就已退缩的经纪商。
在那里，噪声更低，谎言也更容易在反应堆的嗡鸣中被分离出来。
流过那地方的舱单已经太整齐、太排练过；如果我逼得足够紧，总会有东西裂开，而这条走私线的脊柱也许就会像导航网格一样清晰地亮起。
如果经纪商决定警告他，风险更高；如果他不警告，答案更干净、更锋利。

#en: HopeTown means faces, voices, and the kind of lies that sweat through coveralls. If I walk into that yard asking after a nameless freighter from Montara, I will get shrugs, half-truths, and maybe a wrench across the back of my skull. But it is also where the paper trail breathes, where credits changed hands and someone decided to bolt war-grade metal onto a farmhand's ship. If I can pry that story loose from the people who lived it, I might finally understand who Dustback is protecting and why no one will say his name.\n\nThe drifting cache is cleaner, in its way. Cold vacuum, no dockside politics, just jammed buffers and manifests that never got the courtesy of a proper purge. The Specterborn prowling around it complicates things, but that hull is not there by accident; someone trusted the emptiness to finish a job they were too nervous to sign off on. Crack it open, and I get the version of events nobody had time to massage, the raw path of a hauler slipping off the grid toward sick soil and frightened settlements. One path talks, the other shows. I do not have the luxury of taking both at once.
zh:
霍普镇意味着面孔、声音，以及那种会从工装里渗出来的谎言。
如果我走进那座场区，打听一艘来自蒙塔拉的无名货船，我会得到耸肩、半真半假，也许还有一记砸在我后脑勺上的扳手。
但那里也是纸面线索呼吸的地方，是信用易手、有人决定把军用级金属栓到一艘农场工人的船上之处。
如果我能从亲历者口中撬出那个故事，也许终于能理解"尘背"在保护谁、以及为什么没人肯说出他的名字。

漂流中的藏匿点某种意义上更干净。冰冷的真空、没有码头政治，只有卡死的缓冲区和从未得到妥善清除礼遇的舱单。
在附近游荡的幽魂生让事情复杂起来，但那具船体不是偶然停在那里的；有人信任这片空旷，来完成一件他们紧张到不敢签字的差事。
撬开它，我就能得到那个没人有时间去润色的版本，一艘货船滑离网络、驶向病变土壤与受惊定居点的生路径。
一条路会说话，另一条会展示。我没有同时走两条的奢侈。

#en: Gagarin means noise, people, and too many ways to disappear in plain sight. If Vector spliced herself into the power grid, the proof is hiding under layers of cheap fixes and corporate upgrades. Following that thread is slow work: crawling conduits, bribing line techs, hoping whatever UC worker started this map did not vanish because they were onto something lethal. The payoff is a structural picture of the whole route, not just where she went, but how she has been riding the veins of this system.\n\nThe relay bunker is the opposite: empty, honest, and already half-forgotten by the people who built it. Those atmospheric scans do not care who signed what contract or who needed a favor buried; they just record what passed overhead. If someone pulled a copy and walked away spooked, it means the pattern in those flight paths points somewhere the charts say does not exist. Going back there is riskier in a different way. Less cover, more chance the wrong analyst notices I am sifting through erased history, but if I am right, one clean line from sky to that hidden corridor could cut through all the rumor.
zh:
加加林星意味着噪声、人，以及太多能在众目睽睽下消失的方式。
如果"向量"把自己接进了电网，证据就藏在层层廉价修补与企业升级之下。
追那条线是慢工：在导管里爬行、贿赂线路技师，指望最初绘制这张地图的联殖工人没有因为触及某种致命东西而消失。
回报是整条路线的结构图——不只是她去了哪里，而是她如何一直骑在这套系统的血管上。

中继碉堡恰恰相反：空旷、诚实，已被建造它的人半遗忘。
那些大气扫描不在乎谁签了什么合同、谁需要把一个人情埋掉；它们只记录掠过上空的东西。
如果有人取走了一份副本、并惊惧地离开，那就意味着那些飞行路径中的图案指向星图所说不存在的地方。
回到那里在另一种意义上更冒险。掩体更少，某个不该注意的分析员注意到我在筛除被抹去的历史的可能更大，但如果我没判断错，从天空到那条隐秘走廊的一条干净线，就能穿透所有传言。

#en: Neon's Underbelly is the obvious move: follow the stink. If Vector is bleeding off grav sins anywhere, it is down there in the steam and rust, where waste, chems, and people all get flushed through the same veins. It will be noisy, crowded, too many eyes and not enough law, but that cuts both ways. I can lean on Ghost Coil types, bribe a few maintenance crews, see who has been paid to look away when the wrong pipes light up. Messy, dangerous, and close enough to the source that I might feel the Echo in the walls.\n\nThe research module is cleaner, quieter, and a different kind of trap. Here the story is written in routing tables and aborted transfers, the kind of thing that never makes dockside gossip but shapes entire shipping lanes. If Vector carved his own corridor through corporate sims, this is where the first cuts were made. Digging there means sifting through someone's carefully curated lies, maybe stepping on Ryujin toes, maybe tripping alarms meant for data thieves, not hunters. Less blood, more ghosts in the code, but if I unravel the fork he tampered with, I might see exactly which way he is steering next.
zh:
霓虹城下层是显而易见的一步：跟着臭味走。
如果"向量"在任何地方给重力罪行放血，那就是在下面的蒸汽与锈迹里——废弃物、药剂与人都在同一条血管里被冲走。
那里会嘈杂、拥挤，眼睛太多、法律太少，但这也是一把双刃剑。
我可以敲打幽灵线圈那类人、贿赂几个维护班组、看看是谁被收买去在错误的管道亮起时别过头。
混乱、危险，而且离源头近到我也许能在墙里感到那道"回响"。

研究模块更干净、更安静，也是另一种陷阱。
在这里，故事写在路由表与中断的转账里，那种从不出现在码头闲话、却塑造整条航运航道的东西。
如果"向量"在企业模拟中刻出了自己的走廊，最初的切痕就发生在这里。
在那里挖掘意味着筛过某人精心编排的谎言，也许踩到龙神的脚趾，也许触发为数据窃贼而非猎人设置的警报。
血更少，代码里的幽灵更多，但如果我解开他篡改的那个分叉，也许就能准确看到他下一步在往哪个方向操舵。

#en: HopeTown is the honest face of the lie. If I walk those gantries, I am walking through the last place families saw as "safe," talking to loaders who still sleep fine because they never see where the ships actually end up. The risk here is soft: backroom conversations, forged signatures, LIST clerks who will close ranks the second they smell an audit. But if I can peel back their paperwork, I might finally see who signed off on letting him rewrite entire lives with a few quiet keystrokes.\n\nThe depot is the ugly side of the same story. Out here, fuel and timing are the only truths that cannot be sweet-talked away. The people guarding those tanks are not administrators; they are scavengers and cut-rate muscle who know exactly how many tons vanish off the books when no one is looking. Going in means noise, maybe blood, and whatever passes for loyalty among crews who live on kickbacks and "lost" shipments. Still, the numbers on their ledgers are closer to his hand than any brochure in HopeTown, and if I want to see where his perfect corridor really bends, following the burn trail through them might be the faster, sharper cut.
zh:
霍普镇是这桩谎言诚实的那张脸。
如果我走过那些栈桥，我就是穿过家属们曾视为"安全"的最后一个地方，与那些仍能安睡、因为他们从来看不到飞船最终抵达何处的装卸工交谈。
这里的风险是柔软的：后室交谈、伪造签名、一闻到审计气味就会抱团的独立盟文书。
但如果我能揭开他们的文书，也许终于能看到是谁签字同意让他用几次安静的按键改写整条条人命。

仓库是同一个故事丑陋的那一面。在这里，燃料与时序是唯一无法被甜言蜜语打发的真相。
看守那些储罐的人不是行政人员；他们是拾荒者与廉价的打手，清楚知道在无人注视时有多少吨会从账面上消失。
走进去意味着噪声、也许是血，以及在那些靠回扣与"丢失"货物过活的船员之间，无论什么能冒充忠诚的东西。
不过，他们账册上的数字比霍普镇任何一本宣传册都更贴近他的手，而如果我想看到他完美的走廊究竟在哪里弯折，顺着穿过他们的燃烧痕迹追，可能是更快、更锋利的一刀。

#en: The figures buried in Neon's backroom accounts echo the same off-lane corrections found in those erased UC models, but now each line ends with a ship, a payout, and a direction whispered over cheap drinks.  \nTogether with the redacted hearing in the capital and the shaken testimony from frontier captains, it confirms she has been selling safer corridors to anyone who will listen, while quietly steering them all toward the same unseen bend in space.
zh: 埋在霓虹城密室账目里的数字，回响着在那些被抹除的联殖模型里发现的同样账外修正，但如今每一行都以一艘船、一笔付款，以及一个在廉价酒上低声说出的方向结尾。\n连同首都那场被涂黑的听证会与边境船长们动摇的证词一起看，它证实她一直在把更安全的走廊卖给任何愿意听的人，同时悄悄把他们都引向太空中同一处看不见的弯折。

#en: From the wreckage, a disrupted signal rethreads itself through the old UC arrays, briefly restoring a forgotten sweep that points away from sanctioned lanes and toward a blind patch of deep space.  \nIn that flicker the pattern tightens: the stray datapad's corrupted routes, the buried analyst's censored logs, the orbital anomaly's skewed jump angles. All of them bend toward the same uncharted well where ships vanish and Starline's edits grow bolder.
zh: 从残骸中，一道被打断的信号重新穿过旧联殖阵列的线，短暂恢复一次被遗忘的扫描，它背离制式航道，指向深空中一片盲区。\n在那次闪烁中图案收紧：散落数据板里损坏的航线、被掩埋分析员被审查的日志、轨道异常歪斜的跃迁角度。它们全都弯向同一口未被测绘的井——飞船在那里消失，"星线"的编辑也愈发大胆。

#en: The manifest fragment tags the same unscheduled service IDs that keep cropping up in backwater logs, but this time they all resolve to one place beneath the lightning city, buried under layers of corporate routing codes and half-erased timestamps.  \nWhat started as a broken slate in the dust, then a jittering tower's ghost readings, now points straight at Neon's lowest decks, where forgotten recalls and off-the-books calibrations go to be quietly misfiled.
zh: 这块舱单碎片标记着那些不断在穷乡日志里冒出的、同样的未排期服务 ID，但这一次它们全都解析到闪电之城下方的同一个地方，埋在层层企业航路代码与半被抹除的时间戳之下。\n始于尘土中一块破碎石板、随后是一座抖动塔楼的幽灵读数的东西，如今径直指向霓虹城最底层的甲板——被遗忘的召回与账外校准都会去那里被悄悄归档。

#en: Each test reading etched into this fragment points to the same patch of quiet orbit, the same stress thresholds pushed just past sane limits, then logged as routine and filed away.  \nTaken with the stray report from that forgotten outpost and the unmarked cache adrift in dead space, the pattern is getting harder to dismiss as bad luck or bad maintenance and easier to read as someone methodically teaching the Settled Systems where, exactly, its bones will break.
zh: 刻在这块碎片上的每一处测试读数都指向同一片安静的轨道、同样被推过理智极限后又被登记为例行公事归档的应力阈值。\n连同来自那座被遗忘哨站的散落报告、以及死寂太空中漂流的未标记藏匿点一起看，这个图案越来越难以被当作坏运气或糟糕维护打发，而更容易读成有人在有条不紊地教导定居星系的骨头究竟会在哪里断裂。

#en: When the orbital relay went dark, half the Well never noticed, but a few LIST clerks flinched like someone had kicked out a rung beneath them.  \nIn a corner booth, a broker reluctantly admits that traffic from certain doomed farms always bent through that now-empty coordinate, and that every survivor who crawled back from the fringe remembered the same careful pilot, the same wrong horizon, and a whisper about an orchard that never appears on any official chart.
zh: 当轨道中继站熄灭时，深井区有一半人从未注意，但少数独立盟文书却像有人踢掉了他们脚下的横档一样畏缩。\n在角落的隔间里，一名经纪商不情愿地承认，来自某几座注定毁灭农场的交通总是弯经那个如今空无一物的坐标，而每一个从边缘爬回来的幸存者都记得同一个谨慎的飞行员、同一道错误的地平线，以及一句关于某座从不出现于任何官方星图的果园的低语。

#en: The altered cargo record turns the starport into the first real fork in the trail; the numbers point one way, the ship's actual jumps another, hinting at a hidden route buried under routine traffic.  \nCross-checking it against the data scraped from that dead survey site and the offhand timings muttered by frontier haulers shows the same discrepancy repeating: tiny course corrections and unexplained delays, always bending toward the same unmarked region of space.
zh: 被篡改的货物记录把这处星际港变成线索上第一个真正的岔口；数字指向一边，飞船实际的跃迁指向另一边，暗示着一条埋在例行交通之下的隐秘路线。\n把它与那座死勘测站蹭取的数据、以及边境运货船员随口嘟囔的时序交叉核对，显示出同样的差异反复出现：微小的航向修正与无法解释的延误，总是弯向同一片未标记的空域。

#en: The decrypted route stitched itself across the map, a familiar grid bent just wrong enough to be hers, and every node along it pointed away from licensed colonies and back toward something she once tried to erase.  \nIn the queues and back rooms down here you already chased dead applications, doctored farm logs, a nervous broker, and a ruined survey ship full of half truths; now those fragments finally align into a single outbound line marked Hearthline Return Path.
zh: 解密出的路线在地图上自行缝合成形，一张熟悉得刚好被弯错的格栅——正是她的风格，沿线每一个节点都背离持照殖民地，回指向某种她曾试图抹去的东西。\n在下面这些队列与密室里，你已经追过失效的申请、被动过手脚的农场日志、一名紧张的经纪商，以及一艘装满半真半假的毁坏勘测船；如今那些碎片终于对齐成一条标着"炉线返航路径"的单一出港路线。

#en: Someone in Gagarin Landing wired this manifold to do more than push waste; it quietly mirrors tug traffic and reroutes telemetry toward the same dead patch of stars that keeps surfacing in every rumor about him. Spliced signatures and familiar timing windows turn scrap yard gossip into a mapped return cycle, showing exactly how he slips in and out of that graveyard while everyone else sees only random drift. From the first forgotten dataslate on a backwater rock, through the carved patterns in a stripped Deimos lot and the buried traces in an old relay, every fragment has been pointing to the same hidden orbit he cannot quite leave behind.
zh: 加加林着陆点的某人把这座歧管接得不止用于输送废料；它悄然镜像拖船交通，并把遥测改道引向每一则关于他的传闻都会浮现的那片死星区。\n拼接的特征与熟悉的时序窗口把废料场闲话变成一张被绘出的往返周期，准确显示他如何进出那座墓场，而别人只看到随机漂移。\n从一块穷乡岩石上第一块被遗忘的数据板，到一座被拆空的火卫二场区里刻下的图案，再到一座旧中继站里被掩埋的痕迹，每一块碎片都指向同一个他难以真正抛下的隐秘轨道。

#en: Inside the relay's dim cargo bay, scratched paint and forgotten crates blur together until one drum's routing code repeats the same skewed pattern you have been chasing across systems.  \nMapped out, those digits curl into a familiar spiral, pointing away from trade lanes toward the same dead region whispered about by salvagers and jump techs alike.  \nIt stitches your finds into a single thread: the lost slate from the backcountry wreck, the misjump logs pulled off that crippled freighter, and now a relay clerk's nervous directions all circling the work of one quiet navigation analyst who treats ship traffic like pieces on a distant board.
zh: 在中继站昏暗的货舱里，刮花的油漆与被遗忘的货箱模糊成一片，直到有一只油桶的航路代码重复出你跨星系一直追查的同样歪斜图案。\n标绘出来，那些数字蜷成一道熟悉的螺旋，背离贸易航道，指向拾荒者与跃迁技师同样低声谈论的那片死寂区域。\n它把你们的发现缝成一条线：来自穷乡残骸的失落石板、从那艘受损货船取下的错误跃迁日志，如今再加上一名中继站文书紧张指出的方向，全都环绕着一名安静的领航分析员的作品——他把航运交通当作遥远棋盘上的棋子。

#en: The signal hidden in this orbit is not broadcasting a destination so much as a habit: a tiny angular nudge that repeats every time someone follows her off the sanctioned lanes, pushing ships along a curve too subtle for nervous captains to notice and too profitable for haulers to question. Its alignment matches the approach patterns buried in freight records on Jemison and the entry vectors of wrecks stripped clean near that forgotten scrapyard, all bending through the same stretch of dark. With this in hand, the chase shifts from rumor and wreckage to a single, shared trajectory that every missing ship seems to have traced before it vanished.
zh: 藏在这片轨道里的信号与其说在广播一个目的地，不如说在广播一种习惯：每当有人跟着她偏离制式航道，就会出现一次微小的角度推移，把飞船推上一道对紧张船长而言太细微、对运货船员而言太有利可图而不去质疑的曲线。\n它的对齐方式与埋在杰米森星货运记录里的接近模式、以及在那座被遗忘废料场附近被拆得干干净净的残骸的进入向量吻合，全都弯经同一片黑暗。\n有了它，追查便从传言与残骸转向一条共享的单一轨迹——每一艘失踪的飞船似乎都在消失前描过它。

#en: The rooftop calculations match the orbital anomaly exactly; lines etched in Neon's haze now echo in the cold vacuum above, a repeating kink in space that no official chart admits exists. By tracing where those bent approach vectors finally converge, the hunt shifts from guessing his routes to following the single shared destination they all imply, somewhere far beyond regulated lanes.  \n\nThe scattered datapad in the hinterlands, the buried monitoring logs, and the rooftop drift patterns all describe the same quiet interference in navigation systems, a hidden hand turning routine jumps a few degrees off course toward an unseen point in the dark.
zh:
屋顶上的计算与轨道异常完全吻合；刻在霓虹城尘霾里的线条如今在上方冰冷的真空中回响，一处没有任何官方星图承认存在的空间扭结。
追出那些弯曲接近向量最终汇聚之处，这场追查便从猜测他的航线，转向追随它们共同暗示的同一个目的地——在受管制航道之外某处远方。

腹地那块散落的数据板、被掩埋的监测日志，以及屋顶的漂移图案，都描述着导航系统中同样安静的干扰：一只隐藏的手把例行跃迁转过几度，朝向黑暗中一个看不见的点。

#en: The data shard hums faintly against the noise of leaking vents and distant club bass, its fractured coordinates snapping into place over a map of routes you have already walked without knowing. Last Cohort Vector is more than a heading; it is the pattern behind every triage bay and backroom clinic he has favored, pointing toward the one place where his control group could never be left alone.  \nWe traced him from a dead rock's anonymous slate, through gutted ships and scrubbed SysDef records, then down into this rusted maze where altered patients mutter the same phrases in different tongues, all unconsciously aligning toward the same hidden orbit.
zh: 数据碎片在漏风管与远处夜店低音的噪声中微弱嗡鸣，它破碎的坐标在你已经走过却不自知的一张路线图上啪地归位。\n"最终同群向量"不只是一个航向；它是他偏爱过的每一个分诊舱与后室诊所背后的图案，指向他的对照组绝不可能被单独留下的唯一地点。\n我们追踪他，从一块死岩石上的匿名石板，穿过被掏空的飞船与被擦净的联殖防务记录，再深入这座锈蚀迷宫——被改造的病患用不同语言嘟囔着同样的句子，全都不由自主地对齐向同一条隐秘轨道。

#en: The log threads a thin line through the relay's routing tables, a smear of emergency-code residue that does not belong in a cargo hub, pointing toward a lane only a former rescue pilot would think to use. It names no ship outright, but the timestamps marry neatly to minor "accidents" and quiet claim payouts, sketching the outline of a hunter who chooses his disasters in advance. It is a fragile map, more absence than ink, but enough to say the ghost on the channels is not just rumor. So far all we really had were nudged guidance paths in an automated plant and scattered stories from haulers; now, for the first time, his hand shows up in the numbers.
zh:
日志在中继站的路由表中穿出一根细线，一抹本不该出现在货运枢纽里的应急代码残留，指向一条只有前任救援飞行员才会想到使用的航道。
它没有直接点出任何船只，但时间戳与一些轻微"事故"和安静的索赔付款严丝合缝地配对，勾出一个提前选定自己灾难的猎人的轮廓。
这是一张脆弱的图，更多的是空缺而非墨水，但足以说明频道上的幽灵不只是传言。
截至目前，我们真正掌握的只有一座自动化工厂里被轻推的引导路径与运货船员零散的故事；如今，他的手第一次出现在数字里。

#en: The depot sits at the dead end of a dozen forgotten freight spurs, exactly where someone would stash routing records that were never meant to survive an audit. Rusted loaders and sealed crates make good cover, and the only witnesses here are long-haul crews who learned not to ask why certain shipments changed hands off the books. If there is a thread tying erased queues to unlogged tows, it will be buried in whatever dispatch logs were quietly redirected out of official storage. Up to now, all I have are a stray slate from a nowhere rock and a handful of nervous stories about delayed responses that always seemed to favor the same shadow on the edge of the lanes.
zh:
仓库坐落在十几条被遗忘货运支线的死胡同尽头，正是有人会藏匿那些本不该挺过审计的航路记录的地方。
生锈的装载机与密封货箱是很好的掩护，而这里唯一的目击者是那些学会了不问某些货物为何在账外易手的长途船员。
如果真有一条把被抹除的队列与未登记的拖曳系起来的线，它就会埋在被悄然转出官方存储的调度日志里。
截至目前，我手里的只有一块无名岩石上的散落石板，以及少数关于迟缓响应的紧张故事——它们似乎总是偏袒航道边缘的同一道影子。

#en: The wrecked platform's last transmission unspools into a thin, skeletal map, a pale trace of navigation data reaching far beyond any mining claim. Threaded between routine course updates is a single, deliberate correction, nudging condemned hulls away from commercial lanes and toward a quiet pocket of space that should not see that much traffic. Whoever altered those routes knew drive tolerances, patrol blind spots, and how to make a detour look like turbulence in the logs. Between the dead spacer's slate and the corrupted buoy I found earlier, every scrap of data now agrees on one thing: someone with a shipwright's eye is rewriting where broken ships go to vanish.
zh:
那座损毁平台最后的传输展开成一张纤细如骨架的地图，一道苍白、远超任何采矿权的导航数据痕迹。
穿在例行航向更新之间的，是一处刻意的单一修正：把废船推离商业航道，驶向一片本不该有那么多交通的安静空域。
改动那些航线的人了解引擎容差、巡逻盲点，也知道如何让一次绕行在日志里看起来像湍流。
